#227. Sports Reporter Julie Stewart-Binks Gets Laid Off After Cancer Diagnosis

Sports Reporter Julie Stewart-Binks Gets Laid Off After Cancer Diagnosis

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.usmagazine.com/sports/news/sports-reporter-julie-stewart-binks-gets-laid-off-after-announcing-cancer-diagnosis-it-really-sucks/

Sports Reporter Julie Stewart-Binks is delivering an empowering message to her fans about being laid off by regional sports network SNY weeks after undergoing skin cancer treatment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “your job and your workplace is not your identity and don’t you ever forget that,” stewart-binks, 39, insisted via a tuesday, november 10, instagram reel. “Don’t give them the power over who you are. ”.

The Canadian reporter — who hosted Honda SportsNite for SNY — was reportedly one of several staffers impacted when executives cancelled Baseball Night in New York and SportsNite, in addition to revamping the company’s website to focus less on original content.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this particular layoff happened friday at sny,” stewart-binks confirmed. “This is a place I’ve been a contributor as a host, reporter, and opinionist for the last seven years. While it affects me, hundreds of other people have been affected more — I see you all and I empathize deeply with having your livelihood ripped away from you. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, she continued, “i’ve been through this song and dance in many different ways. Rather than pretending I’m amazing, that nothing is wrong with me, and that life is always perfect (one of the big reasons this app sucks) I know my journey here is about being honest, vulnerable, and saying the quiet part out loud (trying to make your time on here make you feel less like crap). ”.

Stewart-Binks recalled feeling a range of emotions after finding out she’d lost her job via a New York Times article about the layoffs.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “in all honesty, it really sucks for a lot of people,” she acknowledged. ‘It’s just part of the business. ’ But it turns out, part of the business is wondering how many American holidays you have to work to be invited to the holiday party until you get a message from your former agent that says FYI and it’s a link to a New York Times article where it says you don’t have a job anymore. “In sports broadcasting, we spend most of our time talking about this, athletes being cut, waived, released. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the journalist likened the sports media landscape to a game of “musical chairs [where] someone keeps taking the chairs away mid-song. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, despite her personal career setback, stewart-binks pointed out that being laid off is “more common than we think. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “there’s no one right way to navigate what comes next,” she noted. “If you’re in this chapter too, I see you. ”.

When the job cuts were announced earlier this week, a SNY spokesperson told the New York Times that the network is undergoing structural and programming changes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “as part of our regular review of our business, operations and programming, sny has decided to cease broadcasting baseball night in new york and sportsnite,” a sny statement read. Ongoing coverage of the Mets and New York sports are at the heart of SNY’s business, and we remain focused on continuing to deliver high-quality content to our passionate fans. “We are grateful to those team members that helped bring these programs to fans for many years. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, meanwhile, stewart-binks explained a recent onair absence in october by sharing that she’d undergone “a mohs surgery to remove squamous cell carcinoma from my nose. ” The procedure removes thin layers of skin in hopes of eliminating cancerous cells without disrupting healthy skin around it, per the Mayo Clinic.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i thought it was a pimple that wouldn’t go away, turns out it was cancer,” she tweeted on october 7. “I share this so that hopefully it inspires others to get checked if something feels/looks off. ”.

The TV host disclosed that her surgeon “grafted part of my ear” onto her nose as part of the Mohs operation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i’ve played hockey my entire life, but never felt more like a hockey player than i do now. Sew me up and put me in coach,” she joked.

Aside from her work with SNY, Stewart-Binks covered the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics for the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation in February, in addition to reporting for Barstool, TNT, ESPN and Fox Sports.

Diungkapkan bahwa princess diana had a keen sense of style. It was a talent the late princess (who arrived at court at a very young age and was therefore still unfamiliar with the ins and outs of high fashion) developed over the years with the help of experts in the field—and which has repeatedly earned her the title of style icon.

It comes as no surprise, then, that her keen eye for new trends and her passion for the most sought-after pieces were also reflected in the fashion choices she made for her two children, Prince William and Prince Harry, whom she loved to dress alike from a very young age, no matter the occasion.

Sebagaimana diketahui, prince charles and princess diana with their sons, william and harry. July 1986.

Diungkapkan bahwa princess diana, it must be said, was neither the first nor the last mother to choose identical outfits for her children, but it seems this habit was not merely a fashion game. According to a report by Marie Claire, the princess’s former butler, Paul Burrell, reportedly said that Diana’s choice to dress William and Harry identically was a way to reinforce the idea that, in her eyes, there was no difference between the two—even though everyone around her showed preferential treatment toward the eldest son, the future heir to the throne.

Diungkapkan bahwa princess diana with her sons, william and harry. August 1986.

Berdasarkan laporan, that’s why the princess waged her own battle, even choosing to dress her two sons in matching outfits, almost as if to convey a sense of unity and equality in their appearance. If these were indeed some of the reasons behind the brothers’ identical looks, it certainly wouldn’t be surprising. We know full well how Diana insisted on equal treatment for her two sons, who, for their part, apparently didn’t much care for their mother’s tendency to choose identical outfits. “The boys hated that, by the way; they didn’t want to be dressed the same,” Burrell added.

Sebagaimana diketahui, princess diana with her sons, william and harry. July 1988.

Berdasarkan laporan, this statement has also been confirmed by prince harry himself. The younger son said with a smile: “I genuinely think she got satisfaction out of dressing myself and William up in the most bizarre outfits—normally matching. In the 2017 television documentary, Diana, Our Mother: Her Life and Legacy, which aired on the 20th anniversary of Princess Diana’s death, her two sons spoke openly about their mother. It was weird shorts and little shiny shoes with the old clip-on. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, princess diana with her sons, william and harry. August 1989.

Berdasarkan laporan, bermuda shorts and patent leather shoes with straps—all the rage in the ’80s and ’90s—were, in fact, two of the key elements of the outfits diana put together for her boys. The lineup also included matching shirts, polos, and sweaters. “Looking back at the photos, it just makes me laugh, and I think, ‘How could you do that to us?’” Harry added with a touch of irony.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as they grew up, the two, of course, began to rebel against this tradition—particularly william, who, according to harry’s account, at one point refused to have anything to do with being his brother’s twin. Why do I have to be dressed the same as him?’” he recalled. You know, I’m the older brother. If you’re going to dress differently, I’m not going to be the only person dressed like this. “Funnily enough, we got to the age when William would turn round and go: ‘Oh, this is ridiculous. “Hang on a second. This is just ridiculous!” Harry replied.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as with any growing boy, things gradually began to change, and the two brothers started to develop their own independent style. But one can’t help but pause to consider how every choice—even the most trivial, like picking out an outfit—was a statement of intent for the beloved princess. Always in the name of love.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i didn’t think there was any way survivor 51 could outcrazy that wild tribal council confrontation between kilby, lewis, sharonda, eric, cristian and linnea a few weeks ago where two extra votes were played and they all threatened to draw rocks. I was wrong. Last night’s Double Duos twist may have outcrazied that mess, as we got an idol play, two shots in the dark and maybe the weirdest extra vote decision in the history of Survivor. Wrong. It’s that last part I’m particularly fascinated by, as I’ve watched the episode twice and am still baffled by the decision-making. I’m not the only one either.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, let’s walk through this step by step because there’s a lot going on here. If you play your shot in the dark on Survivor, which gives you a 1 in 6 chance of drawing a scroll that keeps you safe, you lose your ability to vote. Cristian was picked to go on the journey and earned an extra vote that was only good for that night’s Tribal Council. With all the chaos and uncertainty at Tribal Council, however, he and Carter, who were paired as a duo, decided Cristian should play his shot in the dark to try and earn safety for the pair. That meant Cristian couldn’t use the extra vote himself and needed to give it away to someone else.

Berdasarkan laporan, cristian has a lot of close allies and is a member of the so-called salt alliance, but for unclear reasons, he decided to give the vote to eric, who is not part of the alliance, during tribal council. He told Eric he was giving him the vote to build trust, and since they do have some history together on a shared pre-merge tribe, he may have thought that was the best way to ensure Eric would vote with them. Now, you might be thinking this is the baffling Tribal Council decision I referenced in the headline, but it’s not. I think it was a weird move, but I sort of understand where Cristian was coming from. Personally, I would have just had Carter play the vote, but I can kind of, sort of see where he was coming from.

Berdasarkan laporan, no, the baffling decision was what eric then did with that vote. He just put it in his pocket and noped out, despite the fact that he knew it was only good for that night’s Tribal Council. In his voting confessional, he said he didn’t think it needed to be played since he thought they had the numbers on their side. So, he just… didn’t play it and let it expire without ever being used.

Diungkapkan bahwa i was so confused during my first viewing that i thought i must have misheard the television. Nope. He just didn’t play it because he thought the votes were already there. I did not. Not surprisingly, fans on social media were collectively confused as well. I saw numerous tweets trying to work out the why and even former players calling out his bizarre decision.

Berdasarkan laporan, now, to be clear, i’m not saying there’s an obvious play eric should have made with the extra vote. He could have thrown a random vote on Mike and Maggie to help protect himself and Thien An in case they caught their own stray vote. He could have simply thrown it on Jelly and Dev to solidify that trust with Cristian. Either of those paths would have been perfectly fine, but instead, he did nothing with it and opened himself up to possible problems with Cristian.

Diungkapkan bahwa everyone knows how many votes were cast last night. Maybe they make it a thing. Maybe they don’t. They can all count; so, in theory, Cristian and Carter should be able to figure out that Eric just put the extra vote in his pocket. Either way, it seems like a wild gamble to take when the vote has no practical value and at least Cristian and Carter and perhaps more players in that alliance can call him out later if he tries to pretend like it’s a real vote as a leverage move later in the game.

Diungkapkan bahwa i can’t wait to get a full explanation from eric whenever he does pregame press about why he didn’t use the extra vote. In a perfect world, we'll even get a confessional about it in the edit next week. Regardless of his reasons though, his decision will go down as yet another example of why this season of Survivor has been the best in a long time, at least so far. The scheming is incessant, and production has mostly found the right balance between twists and getting out of the way. The castaways are all over the top and ridiculous. I can’t wait to see how it all concludes.

I felt stricken to see his hands and arms badly scratched and swollen, his body bruised and aching from all the hugs and handshakes he had received from well-wishers. When I asked him, “Do you think we have a good chance?” he answered tentatively, “It’s going to be a tough fight, let’s see. Stretched out with a bolster under his feet, he talked to us about his punishing tours, and how much he was looking forward to the closing of the campaign. ” Our daughter, Priyanka, and I were glad to tell him that we were confident of a victory for him in his constituency.

Berdasarkan laporan, on the morning of may 20, we drove together to the polling booth to cast our vote. The ballot paper was a large sheet, and I was confused by the plethora of party symbols printed on it. For a moment I even thought I’d have to forgo giving him my vote. On the way back I told him how flustered I’d been looking for the spot where I had to place my mark. He laughed, holding my hand with that gentle touch that never failed to dispel my anxiety.

Berdasarkan laporan, he left for another day’s tour and was scheduled to touch down at delhi airport later, just to change from a helicopter to a plane that would take him to orissa. ” “All right,” he laughed. “It’s just two more days anyway. I’ll see you when you get back. He spoke on the phone to our son, Rahul, to wish him well for a coming test and cautioned him lovingly to be careful about his safety. He had a quick bath and a snack; then it was time to leave. I was excited to get a sudden message that he’d come home briefly at around four fifteen in the afternoon. He said goodbye to Priyanka, then suddenly turned to me, and said, “Why don’t you come with me?” I was tempted for a moment, then replied, “I’m still very tired, Rajiv. ” He was scheduled to return for a break before going on to the last stage of campaigning.

This picture of us embracing in a tree was by a friend.

Diungkapkan bahwa we gave each other a goodbye hug and he left. Some parts remain a blur in my mind. It’s more than thirty years since that fateful evening. I still find it searing to revisit those events. I watched him, as was my habit, from behind the curtain, till he disappeared from view. I thought then and afterwards, many times—why, why didn’t I go with him? My last living image of him is his smile as he looks back, waves to me, and steps into the car that will drive him to the airport.

Diungkapkan bahwa rajiv had completed his campaign rallies in bhubaneshwar in orissa, flown to andhra pradesh for more rallies, and then was going to madras (renamed chennai five years later). That was going to be his last engagement of the day. He reached Madras and immediately set off by road towards a small town then unknown to most people called Sriperumbudur. He was informed that the plane that was to fly him to Tamil Nadu had developed a snag, then came a second message that it was now in order. He’d already covered many important places in the state, but he didn’t want to disappoint the candidate, a senior Congress Party representative, Maragatham Chandrashekhar; she had pleaded with him to stop there for just a brief meeting.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he stepped out of the car to meet party workers who had lined up to welcome him. Next in line was a woman holding a garland who motioned as if to offer it to him. He walked down the receiving line and was asked by one of the workers to pause and listen to her daughter recite him a poem. Smiling, he cheerfully agreed. The explosion killed him and fourteen others in his vicinity, as well as the assassin, and injured another forty-three. As he bent his head to receive it, she detonated the explosives strapped to her body. It was May 20, 1991, and Rajiv was forty-six years old; three months later we would have celebrated his forty-seventh birthday.

Diungkapkan bahwa my recollection of many details of that time is sketchy. I retreated; my head was spinning. Some images are etched clearly in my mind, others are blurred and disjointed. Much later, some moments returned to my mind, but to this day my own memories here are mixed with what has been recounted to me by my daughter and others. I saw a cluster of staff members huddled together, sobbing, tears streaming down their faces, the children’s nanny, Ongmu, wailing loudly. I remember that at some point during that night of horror I dragged myself through the corridor towards the porch and drew aside the curtain on the main door to look for Priyanka. I was about to fall. I could barely feel my legs. As hard as I tried, it was like attempting to read words on a blank piece of paper. I was so overwhelmed by panic and pain that for years they absented themselves from my memory. Priyanka saw me; she held me up and took me to her room, made me sit on her bed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on may 27 rahul, priyanka, and i set out with relatives and friends by a special train for allahabad. They had given him their vote and wanted to see him return as their prime minister. We travel through the night, an exhausting journey broken by frequent stops. People are waiting, grieving and disconsolate. We reach his constituency, Amethi, at three thirty in the morning. At every break crowds of mourners surge forward for a glimpse of the urn containing Rajiv’s ashes. They had placed their trust in him, shared their pains, hopes, and aspirations with him. Instead, they are paying their last tearful tribute to their leader’s ashes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we reach allahabad later on the morning of may 28 and are driven to rajiv’s ancestral home. We place the urn on the platform where the ashes of his grandfather, his brother, and his mother had been placed before. In the afternoon we are taken by boat to the sacred Sangam for the immersion.

Sebagaimana diketahui, two decades earlier, on a pearly dawn, we had set off—rajiv, his brother sanjay, and i—on a boat ride to the sangam at my mother-in-law’s request. Rajiv had pointed out the different colors of the water, the mood of the two rivers, one almost resisting merging with the other. He had explained the religious belief in a third river, the invisible Saraswati flowing below the mighty Ganga and the Yamuna. Finally he had guided me through the meaning of the ritual that we were then to perform.

Berdasarkan laporan, on this day we are taken on a boat towards the sangam—rahul, priyanka, and i. Rahul, with the priest by his side, empties his father’s ashes into the river. A military band plays “Abide with Me,” one of Mahatma Gandhi’s favorite hymns. We reach a platform raised over the water. We clamber onto it with others, amidst Vedic chanting. Crowds on other boats encircle us, chanting Rajiv’s name. Priyanka holds me tenderly as my tears blind me to the scene. We are taken to the shore and then back to Swaraj Bhawan.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i find rajiv’s travel bag—someone had brought it back. A separate bag has the clothes he had changed out of. My heart racing, I open it: two khadi kurta sets, handkerchiefs, a shawl, his underclothes neatly folded. His little toilet bag, toothbrush and shaver, his hairbrush, dark glasses, and a portable radio. I look at them one by one: the children at different stages of their growing up, his mother and brother. In an inside zippered compartment, the portable array of family photographs he always carried with him—the first picture he took of me in Cambridge, and later ones. He had always packed his own bags, whether for official or personal tours—as his mother had brought him up to do things on his own. I bend over it, seeking to inhale the elusive scent of my beloved, gone forever.

Rahul and Priyanka supporting me at Rajiv’s funeral in 1991.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, many of rajiv’s friends had also come to attend his funeral. I met them briefly with the children. We were touched that some of them had come all the way from distant countries to bid him their last farewell. They were friends from his time in Cambridge as well as from his school days and his years as a pilot. It was a testament to the bond that had kept them close through the years.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, my maternal uncles, my mother, and my sister nadia had come, too, and both my sisters’ estranged husbands. Mother and Nadia stayed back after the funeral to comfort and support us. From the time they first met Rajiv, they had loved him and looked to him as the special human being he was—caring, joyful, always ready to cheer up and help others, his beautiful eyes and smile a reflection of his inner being.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at times over the next few weeks i could feel a certain restlessness in nadia. A few days before her departure, while sitting in the drawing room in the afternoon, the two of us alone, she began to talk about our young days when I was still at home before I went to Cambridge—how she always looked up to me and admired me, even though she’d tell tales to our mother on her older sisters, of our games, of my helping her with her homework, of Rajiv when she first saw him.

Berdasarkan laporan, suddenly she became very serious and, looking straight into my eyes, she exclaimed, “sonia, they killed your mother-in-law, now they have killed your husband. What are you still doing here? What are you waiting for? For your children’s turn, and yours? India has brought you so much sorrow. Come home, Sonia, we all want you to come back [to Italy]. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i was stunned by her words. For a moment I couldn’t even speak, but as I regained my composure, I replied firmly, “No, Nadia, no! You can’t understand. It is my country, my children’s country. This is my home. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, from belonging: a journey of love by sonia gandhi, to be published on november 10, 2026, by the knopf doubleday publishing group, a division of penguin random house llc. Copyright © 2026 by Sonia Gandhi.

Who knew the Focker family could inspire such a gorgeous fashion moment?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Diungkapkan bahwa ariana grande has been keeping a relatively low profile lately, but a new focker family gathering was enough to lure her back onto the red carpet. The Wicked star turned up for the Focker-In-Law premiere in New York, and her vintage gown was gorgeous. What I didn't realize until her stylist explained it, though, was that the dress was chosen with the original Meet the Parents in mind. I love a good fashion throwback, especially when there's a movie connection.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, grande attended the november 11 premiere at new york city's beacon theatre ahead of the comedy's arrival on the 2026 movie schedule, alongside returning stars ben stiller and robert de niro. She wore a floor-length, silver-gray gown with a subtle plaid pattern, delicate straps and floral beading across the fitted bodice. Take a look:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you'd told me it was simply a pretty vintage find, i would've believed you. But stylist Law Roach explained to ET that the dress was part of a deliberate throwback:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, well, she’s wearing badgley mischka from the ‘90s. I mean, ‘Meet the Parents’ came out. And you know I’m always trying to bring the story into clothes. 2002, 2004, and it just felt of the era. And so, because that’s the way she treats me. And the dress just reminded me of, like, the '90s and early 2000s, when I think the original Fockers came out. I perceive Ari in a way that is very feminine and ladylike and soft and gentle, you know. So that’s the way that is reflected in the clothes.

Diungkapkan bahwa i love that roach even caught himself mixing up the titles. For the record, Meet the Parents arrived in 2000, and Meet the Fockers followed in 2004. The gown predates both movies, but I get exactly what he means. It has that late-'90s, early-2000s formalwear feel without looking like something the music and screen icon borrowed from an old costume department.

Sebagaimana diketahui, looking at the photos, i think he nailed it. I'm sure Greg Focker would have something awkward to say about it. Grande wore her hair pulled back with a pale bow and kept the jewelry simple. The tiny gray checks give the full skirt an almost architectural quality, while the little flowers around the neckline soften the whole thing. Jack Byrnes would probably demand to know where she bought it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i also like hearing roach explain why he gravitates toward these softer looks for the “7 rings” performer. He's previously talked about the hours of fittings and planning that go into their collaborations, and his description of their working relationship here is pretty sweet. After all the elaborate Glinda-inspired outfits we saw during the Wicked press tour, including a vintage-inspired look paying tribute to The Wizard of Oz, it's fun seeing the two bring that same attention to detail to another movie.

Berdasarkan laporan, of course, grande wasn't the only one turning heads at the premiere. As you can see in the photo, she arrived with boyfriend Ricky Álvarez, marking their first red-carpet appearance together since rekindling their relationship this year. The two dated in 2015 and 2016, so the evening brought another little throwback. The two recently had fans talking after a rather adorable blindfolded lip challenge. Álvarez wore a black blazer, open-collar shirt and jeans, leaving his date to handle the vintage glamour.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the appearance also comes after the former nickelodeon star stepped back from public events following a busy stretch of work. Her return couldn't have been better timed, as Focker-In-Law approaches its theatrical release.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the movie, grande plays olivia jones, henry focker's girlfriend, played by skyler gisondo. Stiller has even teased how much fun Grande and De Niro are together on screen. Stiller's Greg isn't particularly thrilled with her, while De Niro's famously intimidating Jack seems to think she's wonderful. That's quite a reversal from the original movie, and I'm curious to see how Grande handles herself in the middle of it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, focker-in-law arrives in theaters november 25. For now, though, I'm still thinking about that dress. Leave it to Law Roach to find a little Meet the Parents nostalgia hiding in a vintage gown.

#236. Exclusive: ‘Breaking Bad’ Star RJ Mitte, in His Own Words

📅 10 Nov 2026

Exclusive: ‘Breaking Bad’ Star RJ Mitte, in His Own Words

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/breaking-bad-oral-history-rj-mitte

Sebagaimana diketahui, for those of us who managed to land a role on breaking bad, the show is a formative part of our lives. It represented a chance to work on what is now considered one of the best shows TV has ever seen, and the cast and crew forged an unbreakable bond. RJ Mitte was part of the show’s heartbeat. When I spoke to him for this book, we reflected on our days shooting in New Mexico fondly.

Diungkapkan bahwa i’ll always remember him as a young kid—bright, talented, and a real sweetheart—who was so thrilled to be on set with us that it reminded us how lucky we all were. Rest in peace, RJ. We'll all miss him dearly. —Dean Norris.

Berdasarkan laporan, the last person to join the white family was rj mitte, cast in the role of walt jr. , a comparatively minor character among the core cast, took so long. had cerebral palsy, albeit a relatively minor case. , aka “Flynn. ” RJ, who was only fourteen years old at the time, joined the project after we had already begun filming the pilot, following multiple rounds of auditions stretching out over several months. Well, it was about verisimilitude. You might wonder why casting Walt Jr. As written, Walt Jr. It was a fundamental part of the character, and Vince was adamant that the role not be played by a nondisabled actor.

Sebagaimana diketahui, vince gilligan, creator: i was worried at the beginning that people wouldn’t connect with walt. They’d say, Why is this guy doing this terrible thing? And so I kind of loaded him up for bear in terms of, you know, he had a son with cerebral palsy. You felt bad for him. People bullied him.

Diungkapkan bahwa sharon bialy, casting director: we had a lot of autonomy with casting, once we knew what vince was looking for, once we all agreed that, aesthetically, we were talking about the same type of actor. Vince only wanted actors who had CP. A case in point is RJ Mitte’s role. So, we conducted a nationwide search.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rj mitte, walt jr. So, Vince was really particular about the role of Walt Jr. is actually based on a real person, a friend of Vince’s from college who had cerebral palsy. : Walt Jr. and who was going to play him.

Sebagaimana diketahui, experienced actors who also have mild cp is not the deepest pool, of course, but there are more candidates than you might expect. And RJ Mitte’s casting has to be considered something of a surprise, given his relative lack of experience and a variety of other challenges he faced while growing up.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rj mitte: we were living in houston when my sister got discovered at a water park, and that’s what brought us to la. It was a paid trip. We really didn’t have a lot going on. My mom was a single mom, and she had recently been partially paralyzed in a car accident, and my grandparents, who I was very close to, were both sick and dying, so when we got this offer to go to LA, we took it. She was one and a half at the time. They put us up in a motel in Hollywood—there was a strip club on one side, and a Ralphs and a library on the other side. Things were tough. My sister got booked on a job at Universal Studios for an ad campaign. That’s LA.

Berdasarkan laporan, everything was covered for six months, so i just started acting to meet kids my own age and have a little extra cash while we were there. I would like to think I grew up with a strong work ethic. So, when we got to LA, I hit the ground running. I started working at a young age, not in the acting industry, but with my uncle and family jobs and stuff to make money as a young kid. And it ended up turning into a career for me. Within the first six months, I was on shows like Hannah Montana, Everybody Hates Chris, Weeds, Seventh Heaven, Drillbit Taylor, Epic Movie—­ all as an extra. I think that really helped prepare me for Breaking Bad, just with the quality of work and the type of professionalism that the set had. I’m very grateful, because if I did not get Breaking Bad, I wouldn’t have an acting career.

Diungkapkan bahwa at any number of points along the journey, rj’s dream could have died. It’s hard enough for a known actor to land a role in a show of this quality, but for a newcomer, it must have been daunting, although you never would have known it by the way he carried himself on set.

Diungkapkan bahwa rj mitte: funny story: my very first audition ever in my career was an anti­ meth campaign for the state of california. The description of the role literally said, “dark hair, big eyebrows, and mild cerebral palsy. It was a wild PSA, and I ended up not getting it. A year or so later, I started auditioning for Breaking Bad. ” And I was like, that’s me!.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sharon bialy called me in, and i already had been on quite a few auditions by that point, and i didn’t book any of them, so i knew what rejection felt like. I had a sense of, Don’t hold your breath. But I’m a firm believer that you go in owning it and when you walk out, don’t look back. Every callback was a little more like, Wait, I’m actually still in the running.

Sebagaimana diketahui, walt jr. had a somewhat more severe case of CP than RJ, who did not use assistive devices for mobility in real life.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rj mitte: when i went in for my first audition, sharon was there, and she had hurt her foot. So, she actually handed me her crutches that she was using for the audition. Six months went by, four callbacks, four auditions, and in that final one, they’re like, Okay, we’re sending you. m. The next day I was on a 6 a. flight to audition for Vince and the team. You’re going to New Mexico. Then he excused me for a moment and brought me back in to do my test screening with Anna and Bryan.

Berdasarkan laporan, think about that. RJ was fourteen years old and trying to land a job that would change his life, a job that would help him support his entire family. Talk about pressure.

Diungkapkan bahwa rj mitte: i think in life i’ve always had pressure. And so when it came to doing the scene with Anna and Bryan, it really felt like a family. I can only do what I can do. But it always kind of felt like I was part of the team to some degree, even when I wasn’t. It really didn’t stand out to me too much. It was like, Oh, yeah, this feels right. And so as long as I’m doing my best, that’s what matters. Apparently, they must have had the same feeling because they hired me.

Like everyone else, RJ made the most of his opportunity and crafted a fully formed portrait of an adolescent at the center of a family storm; one whose disability may have helped shape him but did not define who he was.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rj mitte: this was the first time i think people really saw a character with a disability who wasn’t disabled. There’s nothing he couldn’t do that other kids were doing. It wasn’t about the disability, and that’s something that I think Vince really stressed: it’s not about his disability; it’s about being a part of the family and living with it.

Berdasarkan laporan, five seasons in, breaking bad reached its apotheosis with the monumental episode “ozymandias,” in which walter white’s house of cards comes crashing down. It’s also the episode where Flynn learns the truth about his father’s double life, and that Walt has led my character—his brother-in-law, Hank—to his death. The episode builds to a climactic moment where Flynn’s mother, Skyler, grabs a knife and brandishes it at her husband.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rian johnson, director, “ozymandias”: the actual fight itself, i remember being surprisingly fun to shoot—­just making sure to give anna and bryan the space that they needed to find it. I think RJ also did a terrific job in that moment—­ he’s kind of the linchpin of the whole thing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it is indeed flynn who rises to the occasion. When Walt wrestles the knife away from Skyler, his son jumps on top of him and throws him across the room. He’s a big kid, strong enough to handle Walt despite his disability; strong enough to protect his mother.

Diungkapkan bahwa rj mitte: it was very intense to shoot. ” And I was like, “Oh, I’m so sorry. I just got caught up in the moment. At the same time, we’re professionals. Everything was very choreographed. There was one moment when we first started, I got so heated, and so into it, that I kind of accidentally grabbed Bryan the wrong way and kind of like tossed him. And everyone was like, “Whoa, RJ! You can’t throw him like that. wrong. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rian johnson: when you see walt jr. turn, then you know it’s truly over. And Bryan’s reaction to that just breaks my heart every time I see it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the series’s penultimate episode, walt clandestinely calls flynn at school. The package contains money, one hundred thousand dollars—­the most he could stuff into one box. A package is on its way, he says, to be delivered to the home of one of Flynn’s friends. “I wanted to give you so much more, but this is all I could do,” Walt explains, leaning into the pay phone as Flynn listens, wordlessly, on the other end.

Diungkapkan bahwa rj mitte: i remember at the time we were shooting that scene it was in this school-slash-doctor’s-office that we were using. I’m a believer that in life, there’s always a moment where you have to choose to either be an adult or to stay a child. Bryan was in the room with me when we did this part. It definitely was heartbreaking to have to feel that way about someone that I admire. And I think that’s what Junior felt as well. This moment comes in many different forms, but it comes down to that moment where you say, Am I going to accept this and give them what they want and be submissive, and still have that child aspect of who I am? Or am I going to take charge and become the person that I need to be—­ the man, the adult?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rj does some terrific wordless acting in this scene, wrestling with this decision. Then he speaks: “Just shut up! Just stop it. I don’t want anything from you. Stop it. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “you need this money,” walt says. It can’t all be for nothing. “Your mother needs this money. ”.

Yes, it can, as Flynn makes abundantly clear.

Diungkapkan bahwa rj mitte: a lot of the decisions i made for junior were based on my own experiences as a young adult. At the time I was still a child, but I utilized those moments from my own life of having to stand my ground and make that decision—­ realizing who I am and what I need to do to take care and provide for my family. In the show, Walt was no longer doing that. He was actually creating more danger for his family.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i think it’s very powerful that walt jr. This is my family now, and you’re not a part of it. had the ability to stand his ground, and to put those boundaries in place: “You’re out. ” I find a lot of young men and women have to take that stance at some point, especially with parents or family figures that live in a volatile world, a world that is corrupt.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, later, in the series finale, walt is standing over a crib, caressing the hair of baby holly as she naps. He leaves and then watches from a distance as Flynn gets off a school bus and walks into the apartment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, vince gilligan: with walt, you want him to have a goodbye scene with his wife. , because RJ is a wonderful actor. We were sad we couldn’t have a goodbye scene with his son, Walt Jr. We just didn’t have the room.

For those of us who were fortunate enough to be a part of it, Breaking Bad remains a seminal event in our lives, both personally and professionally—­ an opportunity to work on one of the greatest television shows in history, alongside people who became lifelong friends.

BRYAN CRANSTON: I knew when it ended that this was the role of my life.

AARON PAUL: I think I can speak for everyone involved in the show: It changed all of our lives.

Diungkapkan bahwa rj mitte: i will be eighty years old in a nursing home and there will probably be someone looking at me through a window, saying, “there’s walt jr. ” And I’m okay with that.

Berdasarkan laporan, when edith wharton was in her mid-40s, she had a sexual awakening. For decades, the celebrated novelist had been stuck in a dull, loveless marriage to Edward Robbins Wharton, a fellow patrician 12 years older than her. Then she met debonair journalist William Morton Fullerton and fell—hard.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i have drunk of the wine of life at last,” she wrote on may 21, 1908, in the document wharton scholars call her “love diary. ” “I have known the thing best worth knowing, I have been warmed through & through, never to grow quite cold again til the end. ” Years later, she’d finally divorce Teddy and move abroad, where she’d channel these transformative experiences into her most celebrated novel: The Age of Innocence, published in 1920.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i was at a place where i said i want to do anything except period, because i’ve done so much period,” says showrunner emma frost, whose résumé includes a trio of lavish historical series: the white queen, the white princess, and the spanish princess. Frost had read the novel and seen Martin Scorsese’s lush 1993 adaptation, starring Daniel Day-Lewis, Winona Ryder, and Michelle Pfeiffer. But when Netflix asked if she might be interested in adapting The Age of Innocence, she reconsidered. “I remembered it was the very first love story I ever engaged with that felt truly adult,” she says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, then she learned that wharton had actually written two alternate endings to her book—“and both the alternative endings have explicit sexual content. ” It was a surprising development considering the published version of the novel, which is full of tortured yearning—there’s an achingly erotic moment concentrated on a character silently lifting a velvet ribbon to his lips—but contains no actual sex.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, her discovery led frost to fall down a whartonian rabbit hole. She learned everything about Wharton’s life-changing affair, devouring the 300 love letters the author had sent to Fullerton. “Once you actually delve into the Wharton archive, there’s all sorts of unpublished works that are explicitly about this experience of being a very sexual woman,” Frost says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the yearning, and the tension, and the longing, and the looks, and all of that delicious stuff is so important. I’ve been really obsessive in trying to capture that, and be very faithful to it. ” But the sexy stuff in Wharton’s archive is what inspired Frost to make an Age of Innocence that’s not so innocent after all.

Ben Radcliffe as Newland Archer, Kristine Froseth as May Welland, and Camila Morrone as Ellen Olenska.

Berdasarkan laporan, as in the novel, her series—premiering on netflix february 18—follows gilded age aristocrat newland archer, a gentleman lawyer preparing for a staid but satisfying life with his betrothed, well-bred ingenue may welland. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, unlike the novel, frost’s version also has nudity and graphic content: masturbation, voyeurism, a narratively important threesome. It’s not your grandmother’s Edith Wharton. But Frost would argue it’s very true to the spirit of its author.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and there’s more to her age of innocence than sex, of course. “I think when you stay just with the male point of view, May becomes the antagonist, and Ellen becomes the thing to be won or saved or rescued. And that wasn’t something I wanted to do,” she says. “I wanted to have these two women really existing as flesh-and-blood women who we can care about. Wharton’s novel is told from Newland’s limited perspective; we only know what he knows, and see what he sees. Frost, though, wanted to make her version a true three-hander. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, to accomplish this, she’d need a dynamic cast featuring the witcher alum ben radcliffe as newland, kristine froseth—who also stars in the wharton-based apple series the buccaneers—as may, and emmy nominee camila morrone as ellen. Newland, says Frost, “doesn’t fit in with this society. He’s straining at the conventions. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, radcliffe seemed to understand his character on a profound level. “There was a stillness that nobody else brought, and you could just see everything happening behind his eyes,” Frost says. Morrone, best known for playing a May Welland-esque character on Prime Video’s Daisy Jones and the Six, was similarly well-suited for hers: “She’s the most fearless actor I have ever met. ”.

Kristine Froseth as May Welland and Camila Morrone as Ellen Olenska.

Diungkapkan bahwa and then there’s may, who might be the trickiest member of the trio for modern audiences to understand. Unlike her fiancé and her cousin, she likes occupying a prescribed role in buttoned-up 1870s society—and she’ll do what she must to protect her perch, without malice or cruelty. Froseth found a way to convey the character’s depth and dimensionality.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i always felt quite indignant on may’s behalf. “Kristine just brings this light into the room. And that was the essential quality for me with May. All she ever did was fall in love with a man who courts her, say yes to a man who proposes to her, do everything right—and then along comes her cousin, and suddenly her choices are be shamed, be dumped, or fight for him,” says Frost. You love her, and you want her to be happy, and not to be disappointed. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there’s no real antagonist in frost’s age of innocence. “I think it felt complex and morally right to keep saying, ‘There’s three people here that have feelings. What is the right thing in this situation?’” she says.

Kristine Froseth as May Welland and Ben Radcliffe as Newland Archer.

Berdasarkan laporan, frost also wanted to flesh out the world of wharton’s novel by adding mentions and subplots about real-world events its characters may have been aware of—like the comstock act of 1873, an anti-obscenity law that has never been repealed—and by introducing new settings like a boxing gym, where newland goes to work out his aggression. They are the music that’s coming in. They are the exciting conversations. ” Casting Argentine-American Morrone as the Countess Olenska, “making Ellen part of that influx, [also] felt right. In the series, that’s also where he befriends journalist Ned Winsett, a character from Wharton’s book reimagined here as a Black New Yorker played by Kel Matsena. “They are the new ideas. “For me, it felt like a very organic thing to have non-white characters” in the series, says Frost. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, as in any good period piece, the show’s costumes—designed by daniel orlandi, whom frost calls a “bona fide genius”—and production design, overseen by jean-françois campeau, are vital storytelling engines as well. “Weather and animals are really big motifs in the show. It’s about contrasting these people with the real, natural world and the weather that kind of goes, ‘Ha, ha, ha, you think you can somehow exist away from nature?’”.

Camila Morrone as Ellen Olenska and Ben Radcliffe as Newland Archer.

Diungkapkan bahwa though frost and her team paid careful attention to detail, she cautions that sticklers may find things to quibble about if they examine the costumes carefully: “our bustles are slightly smaller than they should be in the period. “Totally, I’m sure. “Oh, there will be some pearl clutching,” Frost laughs. ” And that’s without even considering the sexual aspect of the series. ”.

Wharton wrestled with whether she should include the scene anyway. Wharton did too. “And then she wrote to her sister-in-law and said, ‘I don’t care. While writing The Age of Innocence, Frost says, the author discovered that famed Swedish soprano Christina Nilsson did not actually sing Faust in New York in the year she'd set her novel—even though a performance of Faust starring Nilsson was the catalyst for her book’s action. ’”.

#241. Avedon Director Ron Howard On Richard Avedon’s “Creative Courage,” and His Favorite Images From 'In the American West'

📅 09 Nov 2026

Avedon Director Ron Howard On Richard Avedon’s “Creative Courage,” and His Favorite Images From 'In the American West'

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/photos/ron-howard-richard-avedon-documentary

Sebagaimana diketahui, in his new documentary avedon, director ron howard traces the vivid legacy of the influential photographer richard avedon, which premieres november 11 on netflix. “The subjects he worked with on the commercial side of his career were dazzling and beautiful, and he was so entertaining and expressive in the way that he would shoot them. But I really had no idea how he applied his status, his influence, his access to tell this other kind of story about human beings that was honest, insightful, and more journalistic,” Howard tells Vanity Fair.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the glamorous heights of avedon’s career were what first caught howard’s attention. Later, he realized a few of his favorite portraits were taken by Avedon. Then it was even his TV commercials, like Brooke Shields [in Calvin Klein ads],” Howard said. It’s not against a white background…” notes Howard. It so captured the foundational strength of character and intelligence that Kareem carried with him along with his basketball talent. “I know Kareem a little bit. One of these was a portrait of a young Kareem Abdul-Jabbar at a playground in New York holding a basketball “and kind of casually standing there looking straight into the camera. “I became aware of him really in the ’80s. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, initially, howard, who spent three years making the film, thought it was going to be more focused on the fashion and celebrity worlds that avedon inhabited. However, his fascination with photographs like “sad Marilyn” (Avedon’s 1957 portrait of Marilyn Monroe) grew into a respect for the full breadth of Avedon’s career, and his “creative courage as an artist. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the film, footage of avedon and new interviews with lauren hutton, tina brown, adam gopnik, hilton als, joel meyerowitz, larry gagosian, and avedon’s son john, among others, paint a picture of a driven, curious, and sometimes mercurial artist. In the 1950s, Avedon’s career took off when he began shooting for Harper’s Bazaar, Vogue, and Vanity Fair. Eventually, he ventured into documentary assignments and more political subjects, including Nothing Personal (1964), a photobook with text by James Baldwin that captured the tensions of the Civil Rights era alongside a broader look at American life, a three panel portrait of anti-war protesters the Chicago Seven, and members of America’s political and financial elite at the time of the country’s bicentennial (“The Family”) for Rolling Stone. He injected a sense of play and prewar European glamour into his images by drawing inspiration from the films of Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers. At the height of his career, he seemingly shifted quite easily from photographing celebrities to documenting anti-war protests and the counterculture of the 1960s, even when his work was met with mixed reactions.

Dovima with elephants, evening dress by Dior, Cirque d’Hiver, Paris, August 1955.

James Baldwin, New York, January 9, 1963.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, avedon (left) with gloria vanderbilt and sidney lumet at a party for the movie premiere of east of eden (dir. Elia Kazan), 1955.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we tried to reflect the risks he took and the transitions he made with his art and his career,” howard shares. He wasn’t on assignment initially… he just committed. Had Howard made the documentary in Avedon’s lifetime, he would have liked to have asked him directly about the turning points in his career. “In all the interviews, he just kind of made it seem like it was a natural step. But to me, it's not a natural step to stop getting thousands and thousands of dollars an hour to shoot commercials and shoot for the world's most read magazines, and go to Vietnam where no one was really. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in 1979, the amon carter museum of american art in fort worth, texas, commissioned avedon to capture a portrait of the west. He worked on this ambitious portfolio periodically through 1984, traveling across 17 states like California, Colorado, Iowa, North Dakota, Texas, and Wyoming, with assistants and a researcher, Laura Wilson, who helped Avedon arrange 752 portrait sittings. (Wilson also documented the making of the project in her own remarkable photographs and writing. The result was In the American West—a turning point in Avedon’s career. ) In total, Avedon printed 124 photographs (some as large as four feet tall) and exhibited them at the museum in 1985. Prior to the project’s completion, in 1983, Vanity Fair ran five photographs from the eventual series, showing coal miners covered in dust and one lone oil worker alongside a feature on Wagner’s operas and an excerpt of Gabriel García Márquez’s Chronicle of a Death Foretold.

Berdasarkan laporan, “one of the reasons i was drawn to [in the american west] is because my family roots are in the midwest,” howard says. “I see a lot of truth in these images. ”.

Avedon conducting a portrait session for In the American West beside his 8x10 camera.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a similar fashion to august sander’s massive undertaking people of the 20th century, avedon went looking for “men and women who work at hard, uncelebrated jobs, the people who are often ignored or overlooked,” wilson wrote. In doing so he joined a whole legion of photographers whose images have come to define broad swaths of middle and western America. I don’t think the West of these portraits is any more conclusive than the West of John Wayne. But unlike common readings of Sander’s project at the time, Avedon was clear that his version of the West was totally subjective, more of a cinematic panorama than an objective record. He was emphatic that all photographs are filtered through the photographer’s eye, and become their interpretation. Through Wilson, he declared, “This is a fictional West. ”.

Below, Howard reflects on five of his favorite photographs from Avedon’s In the American West.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i asked if that was makeup, and i was assured that none of it was. I mean, wow, this is what these workers look like. This is what was in their lungs and their pores. I have cousins and uncles who worked in the oil fields. [Avedon] set up, and just as workers were coming off their shift, he was getting them in front of the camera. I never had any idea that they had their days looking like they’d been through what this guy has been through on his shift. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the boy with the rattlesnake was the first photo that [avedon] took where he knew he was going to get at something deeper. It is also featured in the documentary because it was the proof in [Avedon’s] mind that he was going to be able to identify moments and individuals that would be arresting and mean a lot on an artistic level. My own dad, to try to get some spending money [in the ’30s], was hunting and trapping raccoons to sell skins to the junk dealer or possums they could eat. It also speaks of that region as a very pragmatic region. [The subject] was a teenager. He felt like this was almost religious iconography in a way, or mythic. Absolutely just a pragmatic way of life there. As Avedon says, he's a boy turning into a man, and here he's doing this kind of work, so it speaks to a transformation. So that image always resonated with me. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the beekeeper is, of course, a stunning image–one that doesn't have that much to do with the american west. I think [Avedon] could have found somebody like that in almost any corner of the planet, but it certainly is fascinating and a tribute to the research team that was working with him to help find him. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the maintenance worker who’s dressed up in a really flashy suit, suit jacket, tie and hat, that just looks very familiar to me. I mean, the jacket and all the embroidery on it, the flowers, I never saw anything like that with my family. This guy looks like he could be a country western singer or could be trying to be a country western star. That looks like a hardworking guy getting dressed up on the weekend. But the hat, the tie, the gaze, the posture looks very, very familiar to me. They didn’t have that kind of flourish. ”.

#243. Elon Musk’s Cybertruck Is Dumb, Ugly, and Mercifully Dead

📅 09 Nov 2026

Elon Musk’s Cybertruck Is Dumb, Ugly, and Mercifully Dead

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/cybertruck-appraisal

Diungkapkan bahwa in march 2024, a tesla cybertruck speeding down sunset boulevard slammed head-on into the beverly hills hotel’s iconic entrance sign just before midnight. Passersby winding through the Flats slowed down to watch as Elon Musk’s statue to his own insecurities—the stainless-steel embodiment of nuance-free American ego—demolished in front of Hollywood’s unofficial canteen.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, every decade gets the iconography it deserves. At just about the midpoint of the 2020s, ours had arrived, fully formed.

Diungkapkan bahwa and now the cybertruck is dead, which is wonderful news. Musk, who’s having a historically bad November, announced late last week that Tesla will be “winding down” production of the Cybertruck around mid-2027, putting an end to the most hated car in America. And it’s not entirely due to anti-Elon sentiment: Tesla’s general sales have been relatively steady, going down a bit as Musk went full DOGE mode in 2025 before rebounding in 2026. People like Elon’s cars. I was going to call it the most polarizing car in America, but honestly, no one likes this thing. They just do not like the Cybertruck.

Diungkapkan bahwa true, its death has been mourned by some—especially the self-selecting devotees who installed bulletproof glass in their cybertrucks before shooting them with rifles. These people exist. But mostly, the news has been greeted with a rush of enthusiasm, relief, and, more than anything else, blue-pilled schadenfreude.

Now would be the right moment in the news cycle for an art writer such as myself to make a contrarian argument: that the Cybertruck was secretly a design masterpiece—some kind of neo-Donald Judd breakthrough unleashed ahead of its time.

Berdasarkan laporan, i am not going to make that argument, because that is not true. No one in the future will look back on the Cybertruck as an unheralded art object. It looks like a birdhouse designed by Zaha Hadid, which I would love to have as a vessel for feeding hungry birds at my (sadly hypothetical) Zaha Hadid house. Not even close. It’s The Jetsons for meatheads, a Batmobile for people who secretly root for the Joker. But I would not want it as a vehicle to park in a driveway. It is a bad car.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and yet, that crashed cybertruck in front of the beverly hills hotel is seared into my brain, playing on repeat like the most unsubtle lana del rey song ever written. It’s a decade that wound through four years of a former president denying the lawful election of a current president, only to see that former president return to power. Even beyond that crash, the Cybertruck is the ultimate symbol of this surreal and cruel decade, one that started with a global pandemic and a government suggesting the possibility of a bleach injection as treatment. Through it all, we’ve sunk deeper into our collective psychosis—one that’s forced us into rooms with our devices, addicted to social media and artificial intelligence, consuming half-real information and spewing it back out into the world.

It’s a perfect world for the Tesla Cybertruck to define.

The Cybertruck arrived right at the dawn of the decade, in what we can now see as a completely different timeline.

Berdasarkan laporan, musk unveiled the car in november 2019 at tesla’s design studio. Head designer Franz von Holzhausen attempted to demonstrate the vehicle’s shatterproof glass by hurtling a metal ball at a window at full speed. The window shattered. Great omen! It was also pretty weird that Musk was introduced by a hologram of someone called “Cybergirl,” who people speculated was actually a hologram of Grimes, the pop star Musk was dating at the time.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, plenty of design press fawned over the shiny new thing—“long live the cybertruck. See you in the Thunderdome,” wrote Dwell. But Wired wisely asked the opinion of an actual expert: Raphael Zammit, who chairs transportation design at Motor City’s own College for Creative Studies.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i was like, ‘oh my goodness! what did tesla do? what did they do?” he said. It’s what we tell them not to do. “It literally breaks every rule we tell to our students. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, regardless, the cybertruck started to infiltrate the cultural atmosphere. It was embraced, very early, by rappers. It was lampooned on The Simpsons. There were countless memes. Weeks after the unveiling, Travis Scott used his personal connections to the Tesla CEO (they did Christmas together with the Kardashian-Jenners) to snag a Cybertruck for his video for “Gang Gang,” a posse cut with the Cactus Jack crew.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, three years later, pharrell williams, 21 savage, and tyler, the creator featured the cybertruck in their video for “cash in, cash out”—rendered in claymation. Bad Bunny said, “Me monté en la Cybertruck y me acordé de la Montero de los viejos tiempo. Offset’s video for “Swing My Way” has Anok Yai sitting atop a Cybertruck. ” Meek Mill said, “They was doing cyber attacks, so I bought a Cybertruck. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the cars fascinated artists too. These artists were certainly taking a critical eye toward the Cybertruck, but for some art collectors, there was nothing ironic about it. I recall with great happiness the perverse thrill of Frieda Toranzo Jaeger’s Cybertruck, a painting in her 2022 show at MoMA PS1. Julia Wachtel’s CyberChrist, on view at Todd Von Ammon’s DC gallery, von ammon co, earlier this year, pictures Jesus Christ pulling an elongated Cybertruck behind him. At least, a specific kind of collector. When I arrived at the convention center for Art Basel Miami Beach in 2024, the first full year of Cybertruck distribution, there was a line of Cybertrucks wrapped around the block.

Berdasarkan laporan, but that’s the thing about the cybertruck: there was always more supply than demand. According to automotive data platform Kelley Blue Book, Tesla moved nearly 39,000 of them in 2024, a decent start. Musk initially hoped to sell 250,000 units per year. In 2025, sales dropped, then dropped again in 2026.

Sebagaimana diketahui, perhaps the cybertruck could have endured the ridicule of design experts, car enthusiasts, and aesthetes with even just a whiff of good taste if it weren’t for the massive backlash that accompanied musk’s move into radical right-wing politics, and his full-throated support of donald trump. No one stepped in to intervene. The cars got defaced. Some owners tried to protect their weird boxy investments with mea culpa stickers—“I bought this before Elon went crazy,” etc. —but no one believed that, or really cared. After his efforts at DOGE resulted in the gutting of USAID and other agencies, along with unprecedented and remorseless mass firings, Cybertrucks started getting vandalized around the country. The Cybertrucks deserved it.

Diungkapkan bahwa there was also a bleaker incident that parallels the cybertruck at the beverly hills hotel: the dystopian hellscape of the cybertruck that exploded on the las vegas strip, in front of the trump international hotel & casino. The man responsible for that explosion served in the US Army, and authorities believe he suffered a self-inflicted gunshot wound just before the vehicle detonated. The Beverly Hills crash was an accident in which no one was harmed—but the charred, deadly remains of the truck in Las Vegas seemed downright terrifying, a vision of American capitalism and greed that had met its grisly moment.

Diungkapkan bahwa perhaps now, with a new era of washington poised to define the final years of this most delirious of decades, we’ll eventually look back at the cybertruck with at least some nostalgia for its silliness, its boxy stupidity, its pop culture ubiquity. If it does linger in the annals of history, maybe we’ll think of the Cybertruck as a roadbound folly of the world’s first trillionaire, and a footnote in Musk’s legacy, for better or for worse.

Berdasarkan laporan, put it this way: by the time hollywood studio heads arrived at the polo lounge for their monday power lunches, the mess of the cybertruck that had crashed at the beverly hills hotel the night before was gone. Almost as if it never happened at all.

Diungkapkan bahwa wicker has been advertised as an extremely sexually charged movie with a hot man made of wicker. The film doesn’t shy away from sex and sexuality. It has a few very fun sex scenes that a lot of hard work went into. I wasn’t sure what to expect going into Wicker beyond some raunchiness.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i was delighted to discover it's far more complex than it's promoted. It touches upon topics of self-esteem in really haunting and interesting ways.

Sebagaimana diketahui, warning: wicker spoilers are ahead. Proceed with caution.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fisherwoman (olivia colman) has always been an outcast in her town. She has no real friends and not much of a romantic prospect. This led the Fisherwoman to accept a lonely life. They tease and treat her as if her only purpose is to sell them fish. She finally decides to change that, but the scars remain from being told that she doesn’t deserve good things, especially a man who loves her.

Berdasarkan laporan, the fisherwoman has a lot of trauma and self-esteem issues from years of being told by society that she’s not worthy of happiness. However, she isn’t the only one with society-based scars. This is why the Wicker Husband (Alexander Skarsgård) is so attractive to many women. All the women in town have them. He doesn’t operate with the same rules of this society.

Diungkapkan bahwa he loves deeply and purely, without constraining how his wife should live. Sadly, this nonconforming spirit also makes the Fisherwoman doubt his love and fidelity. She has seen the men of this society. She finds it hard to believe that she has one who respects and loves her.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i left wicker very annoyed with the fisherwoman. She almost killed her husband because of a lie. It’s also clear that he only exists for her. Additionally, she refused to believe him, even though he has only ever been honest. I was shouting, “Be reasonable, woman!” as she behaved in unreasonable ways.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, then i had to think about how many women and men let their lack of self-esteem or past trauma ruin good things in their lives. Many relationships have been destroyed because one or both people in them let their insecurities grow and create bigger problems. The Fisherwoman is frustrating, but she’s very human.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i really enjoyed the wicker ending because everyone got what they deserved. The townsfolk got scammed and traumatized. The Butcher (Phil Daniels ) got murdered, as the worst husband of them all, and the Fisherwoman and Wicker Husband left with a new child.

Berdasarkan laporan, it was only after the fisherwoman could let go of her insecurities and her awful town that she could have a happy ending. Wicker is about letting love into your life, even when you don’t think you deserve it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the fisherwoman creates a husband who loves her completely, but she also learns to love herself in the process. Find love within yourself, and the right person may find you, or you will at least love yourself enough to feel fulfilled with or without a partner. That’s the real message. Wicker is definitely worth seeing in a theater full of women, or alone, where you can meditate on its messages.

Either way, come for the sexy parts, stay for the self-love.

So yeah, it was important for me to like show that and show what goes down at the club.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for those unfamiliar, darkrooms have a long history in queer history. They're typically pitch black rooms in bars where patrons can engage in anonymous sexual activity. They were shown in the media dating back to Harvey Fierstein's Torch Song Trilogy back in 1988, and Jordan Firstman's movie brings them back to the big screen in a more modern context.

Diungkapkan bahwa in a drug-fueled haze peter has sex with a woman early in club kid in a darkroom, and that unknowingly gets her pregnant. That's how his son Arlo ends up dropped at his door over a decade later, with the party promoter suddenly forced to become a parent to a child he never knew existed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there's been a ton of chatter lately about lgbtq+ movies actually starring queer actors, and jordan firstman was able to bring a very real, niche experience to the mainstream as the director, writer, and star of club kid. Later in our conversation he spoke more about the way the darkroom scene was shot, telling me:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but i think also showing it in a elegant way, like i really love how that scene is shot. I think it's like very classy. And it's not, it's like, I don't know. It just it's like beautiful, but still it does, a dark room does feel that way.

Berdasarkan laporan, he's not wrong. The darkroom scene isn't a sexually explicit scene, despite the setting. Instead it uses light in a fascinating way that's immersive, but not overly graphic. The audience sees Peter decide to have sex with a woman at the behest of a guy he's interested in, and it's that union that serves as the catalyst for the movie's primary story.

Diungkapkan bahwa the authentic way the darkroom is shown, as well as the unique chaos of the nightlife as a whole, instantly brings club kid into a specific time and place. The movie shows what the club scene is like for LGBTQ+ folks, warts and all. While it's a world not all moviegoers might understand, the specificity of Firstman's work ends up making the story universal.

Berdasarkan laporan, club kid is in select theaters now as part of the 2026 movie release list, and will be getting more screenings as the month goes on. I laughed, I cried, and I loved how real the movie felt as a member of the queer community.

Diungkapkan bahwa reviews have dropped for how to rob a bank, starring nicholas hoult, zoë kravitz, pete davidson, anna sawai, and john c. Reilly, and they aren’t pretty. The movie, directed by David Leitch (Deadpool 2, The Fall Guy), hits the 2026 movie schedule this week. The reviews are not as uniformly negative as they were for another Amazon MGM movie, 2025’s War of the Worlds (How to Rob a Bank is hovering just south of 50% on Rotten Tomatoes), but they are giving me the same vibes. That’s not a good thing.

Berdasarkan laporan, even in some of the more positive reviews, writers aren’t impressed by the heist movie’s seemingly ham-fisted attempt to bring the classic heist movie genre into the 2020s in its presentation (and political message), just like war of the worlds attempted (poorly) to update that classic sci-fi story with amazon drones and ice cube responding to text messages for an entire movie. Caroline Siede, writing for Decoding Everything, says:.

How to Rob a Bank wants to be a rallying cry for social revolution via internet community building, but it winds up feeling more like a mindless TikTok scroll.

Diungkapkan bahwa even the more positive reviews, like cortlyn kelly's 2. 5-star review for Roger Ebert, call attention to this:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, breaking the silver-screen barrier, the ringleader, ryan (hoult), addresses his audience by stating how important they are; almost like a double entendre, the movie speaks to both its fictional audience and those in the theater. This focus on the audience is intriguing, adding depth to an otherwise standard money-heist flick. Pandering to a younger generation by contentifying the plot makes it easy for ‘How to Rob a Bank’ to one day be screened as a 212-part TikTok series.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the same can be said for the positive-ish review from the hollywood reporter, which is pretty harsh on the social media aspects of the film. Writer David Rooney says:.

While the robberies are diverting enough and the YouTube inserts splashed with pop-up graphics, the fun wears a bit thin, which makes the shift into trauma and pathos a welcome one, even if the transition might have been smoother.

The Globe and Mail’s review of How to Rob a Bank also questions the presentation of the movie in social media form, with film critic Radheyan Simonpillai writing:.

Berdasarkan laporan, this is not a heist movie. It’s the online hack to a heist movie, curiously made for the big screen, seeking the path of least resistance to constant dopamine hits. We’re foregoing all the labour of a heist movie because it would likely be oh so tedious for the movie’s target audience, presumably the generation under 30, whose work ethic is constantly called into question.

The fact that How to Rob A Bank also tried to make an anti-establishment, anti-banking movie while being financed by Amazon isn’t helping its case, per some reviews.

For example, in his 2-star review for The Guardian, Benjamin Lee wrote that not only does the movie feel like it was put together by someone trying to nail the “right now” of social media and missing badly, but the political message is also lost:.

It’s a little hard to stomach an anti-capitalism screed not only funded by Amazon but featuring several scenes of lame, please-aim-logo-towards-camera, product placement (after one dismantles the system, a refreshing can of Mountain Dew really does hit the spot).

Writing for The Daily Beast, Nick Schager puts the film’s attempt at a political statement even more succinctly:.

Their film attempts to rage against the machine from within the (Amazon/MGM) machine.

Diungkapkan bahwa in fact, amazon and its ceo, jeff bezos, find themselves at the heart of a lot of the negative reviews. William Bibbiani at The Wrap writes:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s an amazon-mgm production, which makes the film’s efforts to sell anti-capitalism as entertainment hypocritical, laughable and insulting. It’s a film that says you should stand up to Jeff Bezos, but only after you pay Jeff Bezos. No matter how cool “Atomic Blonde” director David Leitch tries to make bank robbing look, this is the opposite of cool.

Berdasarkan laporan, i would like to note that not all of the reviews are scathing, but none are overwhelmingly positive, either. The movie seems like it delivers on action for many reviews (though some didn’t like it), but the great action sequences don’t seem to save it from itself, even if some reviews found How to Rob a Bank fun enough.

Berdasarkan laporan, the movie also doesn’t look like it’ll be all that big of a hit at the box office, meaning it’ll likely be available to watch with a prime subscription pretty quickly. We’ll have to see on that.
