Berdasarkan laporan, exclusive: watch out oscar. Spider-Man is aiming to get your attention.

Berdasarkan laporan, sony pictures and marvel‘s spider-man: brand new day is about to launch an all-out campaign to land a spot in the best picture race at the 99th annual academy awards. Can the highest-grossing movie of not just this year but all time at the domestic box office (now just shy of $41 million to become the first billion-dollar grossing movie domestically), land a place among the coveted 10 the Academy names as Best Picture nominees? Tom Rothman, chairman and CEO of Sony Pictures Motion Picture Group, thinks so and has decided to put the full weight of the studio behind the effort.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the academy is meant to recognize greatness. So, to be honest, I think it’s greatness. I think it’s received wisdom. If there aren’t people thinking about it, we’re gonna do what we can just to make people think about it,” Rothman told me this week. “I think it’s also incumbent upon studios who make these kinds of quality commercial films to get people to think about it, and here’s what I ask people when I walk around: ‘Are you telling me that there are 10 films this year that are better than this film?’ ” Watch on Deadline.

Sebagaimana diketahui, spider-man: brand new day, , the fourth entry into the mcu tom holland era of spidey movies at sony, is at 90% fresh on rotten tomatoes, nearly as critically acclaimed there as perceived large-scale oscar contenders the odyssey and project hail mary which are also in the 90s ( and even some of the more arthouse-style contenders). Spider-Man: Brand New Day is listed way down at No. 46% chance of making the cut, well below The Sheep Detectives and a few notches above I Love Boosters. 36, with a 0. Both of those, along with the upcoming unseen Dune: Part Three, are in Gold Derby’s projection of the current top 10 movies with best chances to land a Best Picture nomination. Pundits are basically ignoring the year’s biggest film, so we have to ask why.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, of the previous eight live-action spider-man films sony has released since 2002, the only oscar nominations they have received have been in the visual effects and sound categories, the most recent nom for visual effects for 2001’s no way home. 2004’s Spider-Man 2 is the only one to actually win an Oscar, that one also for Visual Effects. On the animated front, 2018’s Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse won for Best Animated Feature, and its 2023 sequel was also nominated.

Diungkapkan bahwa not one of these 10 films has cracked the best picture race. Rothman feels Brand New Day can, and deserves to be the breakthrough.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i think to be honest, it’s because there are things like gold derby, you know, whatever that is, that just tend to think only about the art film world, and look, i’m an art film guy. I made my bones in the art film world, I’m Mr. Searchlight, right? You know, my whole career, I love art films. But I’m a traditionalist, and I was never for expanding the number of Best Pictures from five to 10. Okay, I liked it the old way, but I believe that the very reason it was extended from five to 10 was so that the Academy would have room to recognize really quality commercial filmmaking,” he said pointing (correctly) to Christopher Nolan’s Best Picture-snubbed superhero movie The Dark Knight as the key reason.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i think wise heads know that quality commercial filmmaking is extremely difficult, and to make a movie like this, never mind the fact that it’s the highest-grossing movie in history of america, forget that. I’m a biased witness, but that’s not me, that’s objective. You don’t do close to a billion dollars in America. But are there 10 films that are better than this film, just in pure quality? I think when you see movies like F1 and Barbie and Wicked and Bohemian Rhapsody, whatever, getting nominated, well that is the very reason that that the Academy changed to 10. It’s in the 90s on Rotten Tomatoes for critics, it’s in the 90s on audiences on Rotten Tomatoes. Here’s the thing: the movie’s great. You don’t have the results that you have, where we had people seeing the movie two and three times. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so sony has hired awards consultants and is making big plans. Stars Tom Holland and Zendaya are also involved in campaigns for other 2026 contenders like The Odyssey and Dune 3 and Holland is in pre-production on a new film, so their availability going forward is not known. The studio plans a “robust” screening strategy starting just before Thanksgiving, including multiple FYC Q&As with filmmakers and department heads. Rothman himself plans to host screenings and tastemaker events on both coasts.

Diungkapkan bahwa in addition to los angeles and new york, there will be special screenings in london, paris, madrid, copenhagen, sydney, rome, mexico city, berlin and tokyo. And, as Deadline teased in September, the studio plans to do a big rerelease of the movie before year’s end — possibly as Deadline intimated with some unseen footage — that will also bring new attention to the film and hopefully inspire those Academy voters who have not seen the movie (and based on my conversations there are many) to see it in a theater.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i think academy members would be interested in this because it’s very significant from a storytelling movie. In this movie there is no giant action sequence at the end. Destin (Daniel Cretton) is a really personal filmmaker. “I think people might take Spider-Man for granted, and not only that, I think they make assumptions about it. That’s what I say when I encourage people to see it, you know, people of my generation. The climax of this movie are two young people sitting on the edge of a bed, talking to each other, and sharing their their deepest pain. This is really the first of these kind of movies that I can think of that does not climax in a giant battle. It’s really the first, when I think about it. I think it’s the first superhero movie that’s really a super person movie. When you see the movie those assumptions are undone. It’s a very moving, quite personal film. This is the guy who made Short Term 12. I say you may take it for granted, you may think it’s just another, but it isn’t. This movie is melancholy in that way and beautiful,” he said. ”.

To date, the only movies even remotely in the “superhero” universe to crack the Best Picture race have been 2018’s Black Panther, and 2019’s Joker, though the latter is really a drama far removed from what is expected in the genre.

So the biggest question is can Sony change the trajectory of the franchise in terms of Oscar and get the point across that the record-shattering success of this movie is for a reason? Rothman compares it to the Lord of the Rings franchise in hoping there can be recognition for a movie that has taken a known brand to, yes, a brand new day.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the academy members are really, really smart, and they know filmmaking,” he said. “And if they see the movie, which maybe they wouldn’t necessarily do, if they see the movie, I think they’ll recognize how extremely skillful it is, because they’ll know how hard it is to tell an intimate emotional story in that arena. But more than that, I think it’s this specific movie. It’s the work that Destin did, as I said, a true humanist director who put character and emotion first. ”.

While slashers, jump scares, and evil monsters (human or otherwise) rule the genre and are often fan-favorite tropes, del Toro brings a unique blend of gothic horror, dark fantasy, and fairy tales to his work, presenting them through a sympathetic, artistic lens. Berdasarkan laporan, among such notable titles from del toro is pan’s labyrinth, which seamlessly blends ruthless historical drama with a child’s imaginative fairytale. Things take a turn when the Faun reveals she is the reincarnation of an underworld princess and assigns three perilous tasks to prove her immortality before the full moon. Set in post-Civil War fascist Spain, ten-year-old Ofelia moves with her pregnant mother to a remote mountain outpost run by her cruel stepfather, Captain Vidal. While Vidal ruthlessly hunts anti-fascist rebels, Ofelia discovers an ancient labyrinth and meets a mysterious Faun. Navigating both fairy-tale monsters and wartime brutality, Ofelia succeeds until her final test demands her newborn brother’s blood.

Berdasarkan laporan, the film explores themes of choice and disobedience through ofelia’s character arc. Further, the narrative contrasts the brutality of totalitarianism with childhood imagination. The feature won three Academy Awards that season and earned a 95% Rotten Tomatoes score from critics.

From the misty seaports of Massachusetts seaports to the otherworldly town of Twin Peaks and even the distant shores of Troy, Ruth De Jong has spent the past twenty years transporting audiences into the unforgettable worlds created by auteur directors like Paul Thomas Anderson, Terrence Malick, Kenneth Lonergan, David Lynch, Jordan Peele, and Christopher Nolan.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “my goal in my work is to always paint the most authentic pictures,” de jong shared with indiewire at the virginia film festival, where the production designer received the festival’s craft award. The town of Charlottesville has a special place in De Jong’s heart.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s here where legendary production designer jack fisk, father of de jong’s high school friend schuyler fisk, suggested she forgo attending the pennsylvania academy of the fine arts for grad school in favor of working on the set of paul thomas anderson’s 2007 oscar-winning film “there will be blood” instead. Sebagaimana diketahui, de jong fell in love with filmmaking as she continued to work with fisk on anderson’s “the master,” and a handful of films by terence malick, including his palme d’or winner “the tree of life. ” Eventually she spread her wings and took on her first film as production designer: Kenneth Lonergan’s “Manchester by the Sea. ” Looking back on these early days and everything she learned on those sets, De Jong said that she believes “a body of work like that is built upon itself. I think I’m constantly pulling from the past, but also pulling from the future. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, whether designing a fishing village in modern-day gloucester, recreating the white house oval office, or crafting the iconic trojan horse, all of de jong’s work comes in service of the characters and story being told. While crafting a film’s world, De Jong asks herself, “How do I make this tangible and alive and real and authentic?”.

Diungkapkan bahwa to capture undertones of the real working-class people in the fishing community at the center of “manchester by the sea,” this meant spending time with local fishermen. We asked if we could use their lobster cages and rope everything, and then we would,” De Jong recalled. All of this research helped De Jong nail the subtle nuances and layers of the region. We asked if we could use their fishing boats. “We asked if we could go into their houses. “You’re always striving to not make it cliché,” De Jong told IndieWire.

Berdasarkan laporan, the first step involves breaking down the script. “It may be a piece of art. It could be a photograph. It could be a texture. At this phase of her process, De Jong attaches an image to each scene. It could be anything,” she shared, adding, “Then from that, I add physical locations, and we start putting the whole thing together and seeing our film. It could be a piece of cloth. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sometimes these images come from the director themselves. Build that,,’” De Jong revealed, adding that even if it was “a flat 2D painting, the colors were wild and it’s textural. “He would hand me some of his paintings, his drawings, his work, and say, ‘Here, this is this set. While working on “Twin Peaks: The Return,” David Lynch gave De Jong some of his own artwork for inspiration. ” These came in handy for the new worlds of the series, like the landmark Episode 8 (also known as “Gotta Light?”), in which De Jong designed the radio station and other eerier riffs on the atomic age 1950s.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for the more iconic aspects of “twin peaks, ” de jong also dug up the original plans for the red room from the 1990s. “David remembered in his mind’s eye,” De Jong said, “and I’m there to continue to be David’s conduit on the new work. It was just a beautiful, beautiful dance. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa along with reviving iconic sets from pop culture’s past, de jong herself has created work that has become part of the entertainment firmament. On the honor of her set being preserved in such a way, De Jong said, “It’s pretty incredible, because in the act of doing it, you aren’t thinking about what this is going to turn into. The set she created for the “Jupiter’s Claim” theme park in Jordan Peele’s “Nope” has been added to the Studio Tour at Universal Studios Hollywood, a unique feat for an aspect of filmmaking that is often binned as soon as a production wraps. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after receiving her first oscar nomination for her work on christopher nolan‘s best picture-winning biopic “oppenheimer,” de jong re-teamed with the writer-director this year for his ambitious take on homer’s epic poem “the odyssey. ” For this film, her process began at Nolan’s home, where she spent hours reading the script. Afterwards, De Jong asked for the parameters. “He said, ‘There are none,'” De Jong recalled.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this allowed the designer the freedom to “take the audience on the same journey that odysseus (matt damon) was on,” she said. “We didn’t care that we were shooting the Laestrygonians in Scotland. It just had the topography we were interested in. Starting with seven countries, De Jong and Nolan began searching for the film’s faraway locations, the only edict being that Nolan wanted the film to start in the Mediterranean and end in the Mediterranean. Same with Iceland and the same with Morocco,” De Jong said. It didn’t matter. Without the barriers of realism, De Jong found inspiration in locations across the globe. Once the locations were determined, then came building sets that reflected the characters who inhabit them.

Berdasarkan laporan, for the ominous stone house owned by circe (samantha morton), who beguiles odysseus’ men and turns them into pigs, de jong shared that nolan “was very clear about not wanting circe’s home to be a hansel and gretel in the woods type cottage. Soon, a whole backstory informed the building of her dwelling. ” With this in mind, the duo decided she should live on the edge of a cliff, finding the perfect craggy rocks in Scotland. “She formed her house out of those craggy rocks,” De Jong said, adding, “We just made up all these stories and created the sets from there. Sebagaimana diketahui, the same attention to character informed the creation of the iconic trojan horse, an imposing image of which opens the epic film. Diungkapkan bahwa “they’re master craftsmen,” de jong insists, “if they collected all this wood, why don’t we shiplap the entire body, shiplap the tail? they hand-carved the legs and the head. That leaves the body all hollow like a ship, so all the men could all go inside and cut a trap door. ” Once they agreed on the backstory for the building of the horse, the next step was figuring out how to make multiples out of fiberglass (and later out of plastic as one of the summer’s hottest collectible popcorn buckets).

Berdasarkan laporan, as “the odyssey” marches its way into awards season, de jong is looking towards her future – and her next gig. With every project she takes, De Jong is looking to push herself as an artist. “It’s that space of being uncomfortable that is how you know you’re in the right place,” she said, adding, “The minute I find comfort, I realize I’m in the wrong place. So I’m always pushing to get back into that area of discomfort. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, thinking back to her conversation with fisk all those years ago, de jong feels that what he taught her was “the act of physically doing and going and staying in momentum,” adding, “that’s something that christopher nolan has. All of these directors; They don’t stop producing work. They don’t do it in vain. They do it because that’s their language and their medium. They’re all artists at heart. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, although de jong looks back at her past fondly, she doesn’t regret forgoing art school to join the movie business. What she learned after all these years is that, “You need to go forward, and even if you go forward and you hit a wall, then just keep pivoting a little bit. I’d rather screw up royally and have tried than not tried at all. Stay open and don’t be fearful. You can’t fear. ”.

Fewer executives will be tracked, and less data will be shared if the SEC's proposed disclosure changes move forward.

It’s no secret that Hollywood CEO pay is often a hot-button story.

Chief execs in media, entertainment, and technology are annually among the most highly compensated people on Earth, with mid-eight-figure pay packages a common occurrence and nine-figure paydays increasingly common.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but those days might be ending soon. Not the paydays, just the disclosures, should new rules from the Securities and Exchange Commission go into effect.

Diungkapkan bahwa the sec on friday proposed a revamp of its executive compensation disclosure rules, simplifying things while also changing what those disclosures will look like. One Monk. Two Estranged Irish Brothers Facing Trauma. Related Stories Movies 'One Sweet Hour': One Aging Elvis Impersonator. The result will be that pay is disclosed for fewer executives, with only the CEO and CFO likely to be disclosed should the rule change pass (no more COO, general counsel or other C-suite pay), while the way the pay packages are disclosed shifts. Movies Renny Harlin, Fixture of '90s Blockbusters, Launches Production Company Focusing on New Directors.

In addition, the threshold for perquisites is being raised from $10,000 to $150,000, meaning that some perks like club memberships will no longe require disclosure, and companies will get more discretion to determine if something is a perk at all, such as CEO security costs.

At the heart of the changes are simpler disclosures, with three tables: “Earned Compensation Table, Granted Compensation Table, and Status of Equity Awards Table” with a particular emphasis on salary, bonus and equity grants.

Diungkapkan bahwa “as applied to executive compensation disclosure, a panelist at last year’s roundtable aptly analogized current item 402 to an ice cream parlor that carries rum raisin and maple walnut; flavors desired by only a single customer,” sec chairman paul adkins said in a statement about the proposed changes. “The proposed amendments would, if adopted, revise Item 402 to focus on an objective standard regarding needs of the reasonable investor, rather than on the specialized tastes of a specific investor. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, executives, investor relations and corporate communications teams are surely cheering the move, which will result in less gargantuan numbers than previous disclosures. Some of those changes may be warranted: After all, equity may not end up vesting if certain metrics are not achieved, and a high strike price can invalidate whatever value is in some shares. Those are things that CEOs have complained about for years: The news coverage has a headline number, but their actual take-home could be lower (or much higher!) depending on the performance of the shares.

The new disclosure structure will eliminate the paper gain spikes associated with unvested equity, and likely to be closer to what an executive really takes home, though if the old model sometimes overstated thing, the new disclosure may understate things, if the stocks consistently rise.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there will also be changes to the employee-to-ceo pay ratio, which focuses it on u. S. full-time employees and could make for more favorable comparisons.

Berdasarkan laporan, and the changes to perquisite reporting mean that things like security, parking, country club memberships and even some private jet use could no longer be disclosed, all of which would be music to ceo ears. Even if those disclosures sometimes help tell a bigger story.

Sebagaimana diketahui, then came “fxck up the world,” and the fantasy took a sharp turn toward the matrix. Green digital graphics illuminated an industrial maze of platforms and scaffolding as Lisa continued shedding layers, revealing a red-lace bodysuit and thigh-high black boots.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for the live debut of “v12,” she pulled on an oversized burgundy fur-style coat and strutted through a metropolitan streetscape as flames rose behind her. Three songs made their live debuts in the opening chapter: “Tarantino,” “V12” and “BADGRRRL. By “Rockstar,” the chapter’s closing number, she commanded an elevated platform as dancers moved around and beneath her. ”.

After the opening chapter’s succession of dramatic costume reveals, Lisa turned up the temperature with “Sweat,” another live debut from Press Play, nailing a sultry dance sequence with her male troupe.

Berdasarkan laporan, the mood became more playful for “elastigirl,” whose intro incorporated elements of britney spears’ “gimme more. ” Lisa took command of an elevated platform in towering black boots, with strips of gray fabric swinging from her hips that emphasized her incredible moves.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the chapter also featured “goals,” her collaboration with anitta and rema, and “rapunzel,” which gave lisa a welcome opportunity to address the audience directly. Moving to the front of the stage, she crouched down to get closer to fans and shared that it was one of her “favorite songs. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the chapter closed with “money,” her breakout solo hit from 2021, followed by an extended dance-break remix incorporating rihanna’s “bitch better have my money” and blackpink’s “jump. ” A lucky few in the pit were able to collect some of the “Lisa bucks” as she made it rain with her own currency.

For all the pyrotechnics, aerial action and monumental production, some of the evening’s most memorable moments came when Lisa brought the performance down to a more personal level.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the third chapter, she became the good angel and shifted the mood with “moonlit floor,” followed by “dream,” performed on a hydraulic b-stage in the audience that rises to the balconies of the colosseum. During “When I’m With You,” she ventured into the crowd to greet fans. The chapter concluded with “Born Again,” her collaboration with Doja Cat and RAYE.

Diungkapkan bahwa “cut u off” and “cobra,” both from press play, made their live debuts in the fourth chapter, bringing the number of songs performed from the new ep to six. Released just three weeks ago, the project provides the musical framework for much of “Viva La Lisa. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “new woman,” her collaboration with rosalía, came before lisa introduced “leave with me,” an unreleased track. At Las Vegas residencies, audiences often expect the greatest hits, but the amount of new material departed from the traditional formula. Lisa used the stage to reveal another side of her sound.

Diungkapkan bahwa lisa saved some of her most dramatic transformations for the final chapter, beginning with “thunder” as storm clouds rolled across the towering video screens. For “Bad Angel,” her collaboration with electronic music producer Anyma, she emerged in a black costume with sculptural, winglike shoulders and thigh-high boots, looking every bit the fallen angel. The ominous imagery and dark theatricality gave the production a decidedly different atmosphere from the bright red costumes and playful choreography of the earlier chapters.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the mood shifted again for “sawadika,” the finale from press play, which brought lisa’s thai heritage to the forefront. The title is a stylized version of sawasdee kha, the traditional Thai greeting used to say hello or goodbye. Its Bangkok-filmed music video incorporates Muay Thai boxing, tuk-tuks and other references to Thai culture, presenting the sights and sounds of her homeland.

Diungkapkan bahwa lisa opened with “tarantino” and finished with “sawadika,” bookending the five-chapter production with songs from press play. For an artist who has increasingly incorporated her Thai roots into her solo music, ending her first Las Vegas residency performance with a nod to where she came from felt particularly fitting.

And for Las Vegas, which has welcomed generations of pop royalty to its stages, the arrival of its first K-pop residency headliner marked the beginning of a fresh chapter.

#310. ‘The Body’ Was Meant to Be Dark. Geena Meszaros Also Makes It Hilarious

Sebagaimana diketahui, maybe it’s fortune. Maybe something a bit more mystical. Maybe it’s fate. But actress Geena Meszaros still truly believes it was a stroke of unimaginable luck that landed her the breakout role of Lisbeth in Netflix’s newest teen horror-comedy The Body. Mostly because she didn’t realize she was trying out for one of the show’s leads.

Diungkapkan bahwa meszaros was given partial scripts during much of the audition process, which kept some of the story’s big twists and turns opaque. But the more she found out as the process went along, “I was obsessed. “I managed to go through the callback and chemistry reads without knowing how integral [Lisbeth] was to the story,” Meszaros says, laughing on a Zoom from her Calgary home. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, created by quinn shephard (not okay, under the bridge), the body drops viewers into the dramas of a small-town all-girls catholic high school sometime around 2004 (you can tell because the cell phones click closed and they’re using aim). But the team initiation ceremony — a tongue-in-cheek sacrament of Ecstasy and a warm bottle of Tanqueray representing the body and blood of Satan — goes awry, ending with Grace unresponsive. The dance team, queens of the school’s social order, has to fill a single spot on the roster, and captain Anya Butler (Kristina Bogic) and her right hand Elise Zakaria (Sara Boustany) pick the fresh-faced and pious “Saint” Grace Franklin (Sofia Wylie) over the stiff-limbed outcast Lisbeth Anderson, played by Meszaros. In the aftermath, Anya and Lisbeth are bonded by a dark secret about what happened that night, and the town slowly succumbs to a wave of religious hysteria.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “lisbeth starts as an outsider. And she slowly realizes that she needs it to maintain her safety. “She sees the power Anya has because of the [team’s] group think. She [views] these girls’ friendships as a commodity. She has to get a taste. She’s a survivalist, in a way,” Meszaros says. ”  Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

Diungkapkan bahwa this isn’t meszaros’ first time tackling a spiritual conundrum. She’s so disconnected from normal teenager stuff — shopping, flirting, texting — that much of what she says is laugh-out-loud obtuse, lighting some of the horrific elements of the series with dark humor. With Grace in a coma, Anya lets Lisbeth take her place on the dance team. Fans of Mae Martin’s  conversion-camp horror series Wayward might recognize Meszaros, who played the offputting Oatmeal Beth. But The Body puts Meszaros front and center, her character driving much of the action. But it’s clear from the jump that she’s the misfit of the group. Meszaros’ pale face and wide-eyed expressions comically clash with the rest of the girls’ perfect blowouts, makeup, and headbands. The series also reveals that Lisbeth’s family moved to the town after the mysterious death of her father — baggage she’s desperate to keep from her new friends.

Diungkapkan bahwa when shephard started casting the body, she tells rolling stone, it was imperative that the character of lisbeth be “unnerving in a way she cannot shake,” no matter how much she imitates and studies the popular girls around her. What surprised her was how Meszaros took what was written to be unsettling and also made it funny, turning Lisbeth into an “adorable maniac. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “lisbeth cannot speak the same language they speak, struggles to read social cues, is deeply traumatized by her childhood, and is sheltered enough to misunderstand most pop-culture references. Watching Lisbeth is like watching someone on their first day on Earth,” Shephard says. “There was really no one else who had the level of humor that Geena brought to this. She is so absurdly funny. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the show manages a blend of high drama and comedy reminiscent of some of the most outrageous episodes of euphoria — helped along by delightful appearances by traitors star gabby windey as the dance team’s heavily pregnant coach miller. “What an icon. ’” Meszaros says, chuckling. (“Every time I came to set and saw her fake belly sitting in its little bucket in the makeup room, I was like, ‘Oh, yeah, it’s gonna be a good day. ”) Related Content Netflix to Release Documentary ‘Russell Brand: Open Secret’ Angie Martinez’s Unaired Tupac Shakur Interview Set for Release After 30 Years Jennie Celebrates Sisterhood on Anthemic Pop Single ‘Someone to Hold’ 'Possible Love' Is a Tragedy, a Timebomb — and the Best Movie of 2026.

Sebagaimana diketahui, lisbeth’s attempt to win over the team gets complicated when the girls start seeing visions of grace, which often compel them to loudly repent their sins. And when people in the town start believing Grace is a real-life saint, a spiritual frenzy spreads through the community, Contagion-style. Yet, Lisbeth’s underlying motivation rings achingly familiar: Sure, the town is slowly crumbling under the weight of a witch hunt-esque fever. Amid the chaos, Lisbeth clings more tightly to the secret of her own past trauma, and soon the quiet wallflower cracks open onscreen, revealing a manipulative streak and mysterious religious power. But wouldn’t it be great if Lisbeth could stay popular?.

Berdasarkan laporan, “when you get to high school, you’re really trying to figure out who you are, sans parents,” meszaros says. Being a teenager is hard, man. “It’s such an influential time. Especially as a teenager, you’re going through all these changes, you’re [always] embarrassed, and people are at different stages. It’s hard. For me, I’ve always been someone that molds to the people I’m around. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, in addition to obvious nods to films like jennifer’s body, the crucible, the craft, and but i’m a cheerleader, the show clearly takes inspiration from the bible. The dynamic underscores the show’s themes about questioning one’s faith. Anya, Lisbeth, and Grace make a kind of  Holy Trinity: Anya as the benevolent father, Lisbeth as a savior rejected by the people she’s come to help, and Grace as the silent but ever-present Holy Spirit. Specifically for Lisbeth, the question stops being about what she believes and rather if she wants to believe at all.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “there’s moments where certain people who are devout are triggering [for lisbeth], because [that’s] a version of herself that she feels like she lost,” meszaros says. It’s extreme. “She’s questioning her faith. And it’s a huge driving factor for the choices she makes. It’s skewed. She’s hypervigilant — and she’s always wary that something could go wrong. And losing that stability, she sees the world as like a place where you have to have your own back. ”  Trending Stories Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters Files for Divorce From Fourth Wife Kamilah Chavis After 5 Years of Marriage John Mulaney Has Many Thoughts on the 2026 Rock Hall Inductees — And Picks Next Year’s Class The ‘You Can See Everything’ Interview You’ve Been Waiting For Dolly Parton Heals the Soul on Final Recording, ‘Torn,’ a Duet With Bono on U2’s New Album.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meszaros is careful to leave many of the series’ central mysteries and twists up to audience interpretation. But the one thing she’s clear about is how protective she’s feeling of Lisbeth and the emotions welling up from releasing her first big character into the world.

Berdasarkan laporan, “if you have to judge her, i understand. She does some questionable things, for sure,” Meszaros says. “But I’m still Team Lisbeth. ”.

#324. Russell Brand Was Sentenced for Rape and Sexual Assault on Monday. By Friday, Netflix Had a Sleazy Doc Ready to Go

📅 13 Nov 2026

Russell Brand Was Sentenced for Rape and Sexual Assault on Monday. By Friday, Netflix Had a Sleazy Doc Ready to Go

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.indiewire.com/features/commentary/netflix-russell-brand-documentary-insights-1235227726/

Berdasarkan laporan, the term that comes to mind most is “ambulance-chasing. ” Earlier this week, just one week after Russell Brand was convicted of rape and sexual assault and two days after he was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for his crimes, word spread that Netflix was prepping a documentary on the comedian-turned-criminal.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, olivia isaacs’ documentary has been in the works for a while. Deadline’s initial story on the project even noted that it “was referenced during the trial” and that while “giving evidence at London’s Southwark Crown Court, Mark Pinheiro, a former friend of Brand, said he had been approached by a producer about the Netflix show. ” Related Stories David O. Russell’s ‘Madden’ Biopic Is Out Next Week — Does Anybody Know or Care? In Shana Feste’s Films, Gender-Flipping Cinema’s ‘Tradition of Celebrating Damaged Men’ Is Its Own Reward.

Berdasarkan laporan, but that the project — “russell brand: open secret,” a slim and unfocused documentary feature that clocks in at just under 90 minutes — was being dropped on the streamer to ride the wave of interest after brand’s conviction and sentencing felt distasteful. How essential, after all, could this be? And what could it tell us about Brand’s actual trial, sentencing, and conviction?.

Diungkapkan bahwa turns out, not much. Isaacs’ film doesn’t get into the trial until its final five minutes (counting its end credits to boot), when it uses title cards to share the conviction news, note that all of the allegations contained in the film itself “pre-date” those that led to the conviction, and make clear that Brand’s legal team was contacted after the Monday conviction and chose not to respond. That’s perhaps the most interesting part of the film’s literally tacked-on final moments: a desire to show its work when it comes to the journalism and attendant standards behind Brand’s long-simmering takedown.

Sebagaimana diketahui, other elements are far less successful, as isaacs’ film leans hard on tired tropes and cloying conventions. Captions frequently mention “[unsettling music playing]” or “[dramatic music playing]” during the most benign moments. Old footage of Brand, from home video to early stand-up gigs, is played slowly, all the better to maximize the sense that something is wrong with this man. Far more effective are interviews with those who were allegedly victimized by Brand, but those are often drowned out by played-out techniques.

The film opens with a typical “rise and fall” style montage, charting Brand’s humble beginnings, meteoric rise to fame, profound injection into the cultural consciousness (he met the queen! and also Tom Cruise!), stumble into right-wing ideology, and eventual criminal convictions for horrific acts the film posits everyone knew about forever.

Berdasarkan laporan, it is, after all, called “russell brand: open secret. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, isaacs’ film lacks a thesis beyond the general idea that everyone knew brand was a creep from the jump. She assembles a hodgepodge of talking heads to hammer that home, including fellow comedians, some genuinely freaked out ex-girlfriends, a handful of accusers (including one who, reticent to appear on camera, is replaced with an actress, one of the film’s most thoughtful choices), and some bizarrely starry-eyed commentators (journalist George Monbiot comes across particularly badly here, zipping from talking about his early delight in Brand and his now-held belief that Brand’s far-right switch is the most horrifying aspect of all of this, oof).

Berdasarkan laporan, most compelling are times journalists rosamund urwin and charlotte wace, who worked tirelessly to investigate myriad accusations against brand for years (urwin first began to look into brand in january of 2019). Even smushed up against a herky-jerky timeline and a loose sense of purpose, the way that Urwin and Wace talk about the precise nature of their work, what they can and cannot report, the women they spoke to, and the ways in which they were nearly shut down (and, in fact, many other investigations of its ilk were allegedly turned off) is both gripping and necessary.

With more time and better access, the film could have focused more on the police and legal minds that helped build the case against Brand, but in the rush to get this out in the world, that was surely not a major aim.

Sebagaimana diketahui, by its midpoint, isaacs’ film turns its lens on the culture that helped give rise to brand, the wild “noughties” when “ladette culture” ruled and being overtly sexy and crude was de rigueur. Women were into Brand! Being ruthlessly unfunny and breathlessly boorish was hot! Also, his dad was mean to him! Diddy and David Walliams jump scares! These are some of the insights on offer in “Open Secret,” and the only thing truly revealing about them is how huge of a mistake it was to let someone as outwardly disgusting and deeply unwitty as Brand get into a place where he could pick and choose his “damsels” or his “whores,” depending on who is talking about them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the film speed-runs through the last few years of brand’s life and career, as he pivots into far-right shock politics and christianity just as the walls are starting to close in on him. Brand may have alleged that his former cadre of famous friends and stalwarts won’t “touch him with a barge pole” these days, but the film’s distinct lack of bigger talking heads stands out. That could stand some further interrogation, too, but there’s simply no time for that. (Well, there is, but not if you want to be a part of this news cycle. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the four-day gap between brand’s conviction and the film’s release is zippy, even for netflix, which has gotten progressively speedier with its true crime joints. In July of 2024, it was announced that Netflix would release a multi-part Karen Read documentary, just days after her first murder trial ended in a mistrial due to a hung jury on July 1, 2024. Three episodes dropped earlier this month.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in january of 2026, the streamer announced a lucy letby project with “unprecedented access” after the crown prosecution service (cps) announced it would bring no further criminal charges against the former nurse, who was sentenced to life imprisonment for a slew of charges of murder and attempted murder of infants in her care following a review of additional allegations. “The Truth and Tragedy of Moriah Wilson” was first publicly announced in February of 2026, almost three years after Kaitlin Armstrong was convicted of first-degree murder of the cyclist in November of 2023.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “russell brand: open secret” will surely capture lots of eyeballs as this part of the news cycle winds down, but what the film trades for immediacy, it more than loses in actual insight. Part two can’t be far behind. Let’s just hope it takes far more time to make and far more consideration to craft.

“Russell Brand: Open Secret” is now streaming on Netflix.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, tv comedy vet michael schur (“parks and recreation,” “the good place”) is worried about the state of the sitcom. As he prepares to launch his latest series, Peacock’s “Dig,” he’s concerned about the industry’s focus on “completion rates. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, but in comedy, he pointed out, audiences often take time to bond with characters and understand what kind of people they are before they get in a groove and find them funny. Shows like “Cheers,” “Seinfeld” and “The Office” weren’t out-of-the-box hits; it took time for the writers and actors to find their show’s sweet spot — and gel as the megahits they became.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i just wish that we were still in the world where you could fail in comedy for a while and because the failure is the r&d,” he said. Sebagaimana diketahui, schur noted that his “parks and recreation” only found its voice at the end of season 1, and that’s when the show as we remember it really took off. “We only got there because we failed a bunch of times in a row figuring out how to get to that point,” he notes.

Berdasarkan laporan, the old broadcast model of 22 or more episodes a season — which only a handful of sitcoms still enjoy — gave comedies room to find their groove, and then created the kind of legendary shows that viewers still go back and binge. “You get to tell a lot of story, and out of 24 episodes, there’s maybe three weak ones,” said HBO’s “The Comeback” co-creator Michael Patrick King.

Berdasarkan laporan, even “the comeback” co-creator and star lisa kudrow noted that “friends” didn’t really take off until the summer after its first season. “Repeats were run after Seinfeld, and that’s when it exploded,” she said.

Berdasarkan laporan, but now, with most streaming comedies topping out at eight or 10 episodes a season, storytelling has changed. I think we need it back. And Schur is worried that the institutional memory of how to produce a hefty load, like those 22-episode seasons, has gone away. “There’s very few people left who have a muscle memory of how to actually execute that. And I don’t want it to go away. ”.

#331. ‘Cunk on Cinema’ Review: Michael Bay and Benedict Cumberbatch Join Diane Morgan’s Documentary Presenter for Her Latest Laugh-Filled Netflix Series

📅 13 Nov 2026

‘Cunk on Cinema’ Review: Michael Bay and Benedict Cumberbatch Join Diane Morgan’s Documentary Presenter for Her Latest Laugh-Filled Netflix Series

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-reviews/cunk-on-cinema-review-philomena-cunk-diane-morgan-netflix-1236752328/

From silent film to modern AI-driven projects, Charlie Brooker and Philomena Cunk offer a six-episode history of Hollywood and its output.

Philomena Cunk is flying close to the sun.

Diungkapkan bahwa the obstinately disinterested host of such charlie brooker-created educational programming as cunk on britain, cunk on earth and cunk on life is turning her misdirected fascination at least partially inward to tackle the entertainment industry in the appropriately titled netflix miniseries cunk on cinema. Cunk on Cinema The Bottom Line We want the Cunk, gotta have that Cunk. Airdate: Sunday, November 15 (Netflix)Star: Diane MorganCreator: Charlie Brooker.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this means baiting critics, who have a greater knowledge of and investment in the topic that’s under cunk’s withering gaze, and baiting the experts whose increasingly implausible flummoxitude — not a real word — in the face of cunk’s probingly incurious curiosity is the comedy franchise’s bread and butter. Related Stories TV Netflix's New Releases Coming in November 2026 TV Michael Bay, Benedict Cumberbatch Left Rattled in New Netflix Mockumentary 'Cunk on Cinema' Trailer.

Surely Brooker and writer-star Diane Morgan know that Cunk and her gimmick won’t play forever, so Cunk on Cinema may mean they’ve decided to take the premise about as far as it can go without becoming a parody of a thing that’s already a parody.

Diungkapkan bahwa the seams are certainly showing in the delicately threaded tapestry that is cunk in this series. At six episodes of under 15 minutes apiece, Cunk on Cinema doesn’t overstay its welcome or entirely strain the credulity of viewers who are more in on the joke than her interview subjects. But the ratio of punchlines that fizzle to punchlines that hit is probably closer to even than at any previous point in the franchise.

Still, Cunk on Cinema offers more laughs than just about anything else you’re likely to watch this month, and I’m prepared to follow the miseducation of Philomena Cunk until the wheels entirely come off.

Cunk on Cinema is structurally simple, as television presenter Cunk (Morgan) takes viewers on a history of filmic media going all the way back to, well, the absence of movies.

Diungkapkan bahwa “movies haven’t always been with us. In fact, for centuries Earth was a barren wasteland devoid of entertainment content,” she observes, walking through a sea of classic paintings and noting, “For centuries, eyes were literally useless, because there was nothing worth looking at. ”.

She traces the advent of photography and then moving pictures, touching on landmarks like The Arrival of a Train at La Ciotat (“It’s almost as boring as Ben Affleck,” she notes), The Birth of a Nation (“A typically woke Hollywood fantasy”), and into the comedies of Charlie Chaplin (“To this day, the only homeless person it’s okay to openly laugh at”) and Buster Keaton.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i don’t want to accuse cunk on cinema of being intellectually nourishing by any stretch of the imagination, but as bite-sized introductions to film studies go, it has some validity. Working her way through her usual assortment of photogenic backdrops, from film studios to the base of the Hollywood sign to various libraries and repositories, Cunk touches at least briefly on a range of noteworthy, properly contextualized bits of history — from an acceptable definition of the Kuleshov effect to a rudimentary explanation of the Hays Code to an acknowledgement of the impact of TV on the films of the 1950s and 1960s.

Berdasarkan laporan, cunk’s droll approach to classic films and the medium’s evolution alternates between willfully ignorant and perceptively counter-logical, going amusingly deep on e. as a grooming narrative and resorting to social media-friendly one-liners like, “Do you have to have seen the first 2000 films in the series in order to understand 2001?” It’s possible that some parts of Cunk on Cinema benefit from knowing about the films and industry conventions she’s lampooning. T. But I’m not sure how knowledgable one need be to find it funny to keep referring to Eisenstein’s Battleship Potemkin as “Batshit Pumpkin” over and over. I found it funny over and over.

As always, Cunk can’t do it alone and she’s assembled a group of experts, from the usual dry British intellectuals to a scattering of film critics to an amusing range of cinematic craftsmen (mostly men) to actual A-listers including Michael Bay and Benedict Cumberbatch.

A key piece of the appeal of Cunk has been tracing how realistic it is for her subjects not to know what she’s doing as she peppers them with questions like “What was The Jizz Slinger?” or, regarding the behavior of Taxi Driver antihero Travis Bickle, remarks that “If they remade it today, he’d be violating Uber’s code of conduct, wouldn’t he?”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’m guessing the screening process for cunk on cinema had to be different from her earlier series and that more people probably had to be rejected for being excessively in on the joke. Moreover, it’s easy to notice that Cunk has needed to shift her style of inquiry in a way that’s interesting, but increasingly repetitive.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if your interview subject is in on the joke, the worst thing you can do is ask a lengthy, ridiculous question based on an absurd premise — the meat and potatoes of her finest moments, previously — because if they laugh or, perish the thought, attempt to counter with a joke of their own, you’ve wasted a lot of rope just to hang yourself. But if you ask a simple question based on a malapropism or misheard or misread title or concept, at the very least you’ll get several seconds of well-earned confusion, and then several more seconds of confusion while the interviewee tries to come up with a sincere response or a joke. That confusion is gold, or as much gold as you happen to find in jokes like “The Jizz Slinger. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, with most of the scholars and scribes, cunk on cinema settles for “confusion,” as opposed to the delicious obtuseness that earlier seasons yielded. It’s good for chuckles, but it denies viewers those moments of brilliance from previous series, when Philomena Cunk would actually intrigue an expert with a bizarre supposition or only half-jesting theory.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s fairly reasonable to believe that a serious-minded historian or zoologist might not know philomena cunk and her thing, but it’s harder to imagine an entertainment journalist or film critic with no awareness of this increasingly long-running franchise. But not impossible!.

Some of these interview subjects are performers, or at least people with years of experience talking to the press or appearing in the public eye, which forces viewers to engage in guesswork.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so … benedict cumberbatch? pretty clearly in on the joke and intentionally giving cunk only stone-faced bafflement. Die Hard scribe Steven E. de Souza? Pretty clearly not in on the joke and being genuine in not understanding what he’s in the middle of.

Berdasarkan laporan, and michael bay? this could be one of the year’s great debates, like a tv equivalent of you can see everything. At the same time, Michael Bay has an ego, and it’s possible he went in with one goal — not looking like a total fool — and that goal went out the window, or very nearly went out the window, in the face of one rambling trademark Cunk family story. Michael Bay has a team. They must have briefed him and advised him on how to react to certain pieces of obvious bait. This puts Bay in a liminal space halfway between professional and cool (as his team must’ve wanted him to appear) and thoroughly risible (as schadenfreude-hungry audiences may crave).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, (disclaimer: my guesses could all be off! cumberbatch might have been sincerely perplexed, de souza might have been playing cunk like a fiddle, and michael bay? well, i should know better than to think i know what’s in michael bay’s mind. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, morgan remains a droll genius, never better than in the walk-and-talk monologue on a studio lot in the final episode. D. The material is so perfectly tailored to her voice that she can get laughs even on flaccid punchlines that sound like outtakes from Brooker’s angry political comedy (see his Wipe shows) rather than from Cunk, who does not feel like the sort of character who would bother with a J. Vance joke out of nowhere. Now Cunk’s obsession with AI and Brooker’s contempt for it? Those mesh admirably.

Sebagaimana diketahui, simply put, the cunk formula still works, but it probably can’t work forever. I’m available for talking head segments and I promise to look confused when she mispronounces “Quibi. Now bring on Cunk on TV. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, gene simmons, whom stanley founded kiss with during 1973 in new york, adds that, “we’ve seen bands that wait too long to get off the road and it’s sad. But that doesn’t mean (the band) has to end. I didn’t want to become fat, bloated, naked Elvis on the bathroom floor. So you have to know when to get off the stage as KISS. ”.

The nearly two-and-a-half-hour KISS: End of the Road film shows in intimate detail that the conclusion of that phase of the band’s career was emotional, triumphant and trying.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, directed by dj viola, who also helmed the 2021 a&e documentary kisstory, the chronicle focuses on the final 2023 leg of the pandemic-interrupted end of the road world tour, which started in south america and played north america, europe and australia before wrapping up with homecoming performances dec. 1-2 at Madison Square Garden in New York City.

Diungkapkan bahwa noting that kisstory was “what we call a ‘womb-to-tomb’ documentary,” viola tells billboard, “i wanted end of the road to be almost the antithesis of that approach. Rather than having the guys tell us what happened, I wanted audiences to experience it as it was happening, from the first of their final 50 shows all the way to Madison Square Garden. ” He and his crew became embedded flies on the wall during the trek, capturing planning meetings, backstage intrigue and plenty of onstage highlights, as well as interviews with band members, manager Doc McGhee, Simmons’ and Stanley’s wives and others.

Berdasarkan laporan, “for 50 years,” viola notes, “kiss has been protective of what happens behind the curtain. After 50 years, that dedication hasn’t diminished one bit. This time, the band opened that curtain completely. What you discover is that beneath all the makeup, pyro and spectacle is an unwavering commitment to giving their fans the greatest show possible. Everyone says they want to show the ‘warts and all,’ but very few actually mean it. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there are warts aplenty, too, including: production difficulties early on that created significant tension in the touring party; simmons being briefly incapacitated by dehydration during a concert in brazil; and stanley suffering from a severe flu that led to the cancellation of nine shows and put the last stretch of the tour in jeopardy. There are touching scenes as well, with the band and those around them talking about reaching the end of touring life. Stanley and Simmons both choke up during the final concert while talking from the stage about their parents and growing up in New York, and Simmons even shoos the camera crew away as he and Stanley exchange sentiments during that night’s sound check.

The film ends with the two men meeting, post-tour, for a convivial conversation at a deli in Bel Air, Calif.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the trick to being unobtrusive in documentary filmmaking is to be ubiquitous,” viola says. “You have to be there for the dullest moments as well as the most exciting ones…. It’s a strange balance, but that’s where the best moments come from. Eventually, you’re just another person in the room. You have to become part of the team while remaining as invisible as possible. The more you’re around, the more people stop thinking about the camera. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he adds that, “the trust we’d established during kisstory was essential. I was there to authentically capture what was happening, good or bad. They knew I wasn’t there to manufacture controversy. KISS allowed me into virtually every corner of their world, from rehearsals and travel to putting on their makeup, standing onstage during the shows and being there afterward when the makeup came off and they dissected the night’s performance. ”.

Stanley says the band was not bothered by the constant camera presence, explaining that at this point, he and Simmons are more comfortable letting fans inside aspects of KISS that were previously kept under wraps — and deliberately so.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it’s more appropriate to do now,” he says. It’s all very encompassing, and always has been…. At this point, it’s interesting to let people go behind it and in some ways, it makes it bigger because it’s such a Herculean effort to do what we’ve done. “It’s famously remembered that for the early years of the band, nobody ever saw us without makeup and that was part of the mystique, part of building this larger-than-life persona. To have a band go on stage 50 years later and people go, ‘They look the same as they did,’ well, that doesn’t happen by chance. I think people can appreciate that now and realize that there’s a real person behind Superman with a Marshall amp. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the end of the road film nods to the past with historical footage, and it also provides a glimpse into the future by showing the group working with sweden’s pophouse entertainment — which acquired kiss’ catalog and trademarks for a reported $300 million during 2024 — on the digital avatar show, which was previewed at the final madison square garden date. They’re very cognizant of the fact that the same-old isn’t the way to do it… and want to make it easier for fans who want to control the content. “They’re infusing so much money into KISS; you’re gonna have theme parks and cartoons and movies…just some amazing stuff coming. “They’re great new partners,” Simmons says. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the kiss avatar show is still a work in progress, but simmons predicts that it will arrive “in the next year to two years, at a place that is soon to be announced. ” Stanley notes that “it’s far more complicated than I certainly anticipated. They’re really putting a lot of effort  into it. But the rewards are that much greater, too. It’s quite complex. ” And he clarifies that it will likely be something different from what’s expected.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the idea was never to replicate a concert. That’s what we’re creating. And the idea was never to do something that was appealing exclusively to a KISS fan; we wanted to create a must-see, so to speak, regardless of your taste in music. “It’s to create an experience and almost make us your tour guides into something unworldly, and yet totally based in the music. That’s not what this is about,” Stanley says. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the kiss biopic is also moving forward, with joseph mcginty “mcg” nichol directing and casting. It’s very slow going; you can rush something out but, frankly, I love being in a position where if we can’t do a film that I’m proud of, I don’t need to do a film. “It’s still in motion, and that’s all I can say. It just doesn’t matter that much. “Anybody who’s ever been involved in film knows you can get old waiting for a film to get made,” Stanley says. It would be a nice feather in the cap, but it better be a good-looking feather or I don’t want it. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, simmons and stanley may have more to reveal at the kiss kruise. Both have been preparing for the band’s performances as well as the Frehley tribute, an all-star event during which Frehley’s band will back a roster of guests, including alumnus guitarist Bruce Kulick.

Diungkapkan bahwa the rock and roll over sets, meanwhile, feature a new mix by original album producer eddie kramer, along with outtakes, alternative mixes, demos and a live 1977 performance from japan. “And I’m certainly open to looking into other people working on other albums and go in and reimagine them, rebirth them. “To have Eddie Kramer go in and rethink things was great,” Stanley says. I’m always in favor of making something better when it’s possible. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa both men have their own projects as well: simmons has dates booked into 2027 with his solo band and produced the film deep water; stanley is actively painting “four or five days a week” and says his band soul station “will get back up and running soon. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meanwhile, kiss is also approaching the one-year anniversary (dec. S. (This year’s Honors will be presented at the Capital One Arena in Washington, D. 7) of its Kennedy Center Honor — and also potentially being part of the last class to be feted in the actual venue, whose main building is closed to the public amid disputes over U. President Donald Trump’s efforts to rename and remodel the historic venue. C. ).

None of that has affected the way Simmons and Stanley view their honor, however.

Diungkapkan bahwa “all things must pass; nothing lasts forever,” simmons notes. ’ Do I agree with the politics of President Nixon? No, but he’s the duly elected president. “I remember when Elvis (Presley) was invited by President Nixon to receive some kind of awards and stuff; I thought, ‘Cool. What you think politically, that’s for the ballot box. President Trump is our president, and that’s it. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa stanley adds that, “i don’t believe anyone ever went to any of the (honorees) and said, ‘who did you vote for?’ that’s supposed to be a non-issue. If there’s an accolade you want to give me, I’m here. For me, getting it was just part of the trifecta, so to speak. I’m at a point in my life now where it really comes down to, if you love me, let me know. We got the Songwriters Hall of Fame, and then to get the Kennedy Center Honor…. We got the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Don’t put it in an obituary or my eulogy. ”.

#343. In Shana Feste’s Films, Gender-Flipping Cinema’s ‘Tradition of Celebrating Damaged Men’ Is Its Own Reward

📅 13 Nov 2026

In Shana Feste’s Films, Gender-Flipping Cinema’s ‘Tradition of Celebrating Damaged Men’ Is Its Own Reward

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.indiewire.com/features/interviews/heartland-shana-feste-jessica-chastain-netflix-movie-1235227350/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, shana feste knows her filmography might be a bit tough to pin down. Some directors like to stick to a certain genre. Not Feste. Others enter a franchise and never look back. Not Feste. Some only like to work with certain stars. Not Feste.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but over the course of nearly two decades behind the camera, feste has carved out a particular sweet spot, regardless of the genre or the cast or the wider world her stories fit inside: she likes complicated women. Not unlikable women, but messy women, contradictory women, women who get things done their own way. It’s a signature unto itself.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “my filmmaking, my history, people have not really known what to do with me. “But I do find that they’re all starting to build into each other, especially the trajectory from ‘Country Strong’ to ‘Run Sweetheart Run’ to ‘Heartland. ’ I’ve always been drawn to women who don’t behave correctly. I’ve always been interested in women who don’t grieve correctly, who mother incorrectly, who love incorrectly. I just want women to have the freedom to behave in this contradictory, destructive, funny, selfish way and be given the same freedom that male characters are given. I’m making a comedy, I’m making a horror film, I’m making a genre thriller,” Feste told IndieWire during a recent interview. ” Related Stories Jensen Huang’s Biopic Feels Inevitable — The Right One Might Be Impossible Miles Teller Opens Up About ‘Paper Tiger,’ Adam Driver, and Losing His Home Before Filming James Gray’s Movie.

Sebagaimana diketahui, another shared characteristic between feste’s complicated women: they may be messy or unexpected, but they tend to get shit done. She’s thrust back into that world after her niece, rising star Charlie Heart (Carter Faith), goes missing. In her new film “Heartland,” getting shit done is at the center of the story, as the Nashville-set drama follows Jessica Chastain as Misty Jones, a former country-singing superstar who left the business after her designation as the, ahem, “cunt of country” became too much to bear. Misty, being Misty, takes it upon herself to get to the bottom of an increasingly dark and twisted mystery, no matter what it takes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i am a mom of three, 51, and i’m like, ‘let’s write about some women who get shit done,’” she said. But when women behave similarly, they could be labeled as hysterical or dramatic or that word, unlikable. I’m living in the South now that I see those women every day and am inspired by them. I want to prove that wrong. “I find a lot of those women exist. We have this long-established cinematic tradition of celebrating damaged men. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, for the (complicated, messy, extremely capable) character of misty, feste said, she initially tapped into her longtime love of film noir. She always gravitated toward the Humphrey Bogart types, she said, but wondered what might happen if they gave those sorts of roles to women. That also fed into the dark underbelly of the Nashville scene that the film interrogates, a perfectly noir-ish idea.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it could have been any city, but specifically this dark underbelly had to do with the music world,” feste said. He had just been arrested, and things were coming into light. We thought, oh wow, this is such a topical moment. When we were making the movie, a lot of conversation around Diddy was happening. It was an experience that I’ve experienced in our industry, and it was all too relevant. And I’m like, it’s always topical, sadly. Whether we’re Epstein, Diddy, Weinstein, this is always going to be in the world, sadly. “Sadly, it was a common experience for a lot of artists that I spoke with. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, but feste is also someone who loves this world and wants to celebrate what’s good and true about it. “Country Strong” was about making it — and maybe even making it again — even at great personal cost. “Heartland” just ratchets that sensibility up.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i wanted to lean into the secrets and the dark corners and the underbelly, but i also will always celebrate the artistry and the storytelling of country music,” she said. So to point out someone who doesn’t deserve country music, I mean, that’s a big insult for me. ’ It takes a lot to deserve country music in my eyes. Country music is like the apex of storytelling. “Misty says one line that really speaks so much to me about what the film is: ‘You don’t deserve country music. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, feste started writing “heartland” around four years ago, mostly because she was really missing the world of country music that framed her 2010 music drama “country strong. ” “My father died about eight years ago, and I found myself listening to a lot of country music when he died,” she said. And I realized, oh, I’m really missing my father. “In the years after he died, going back to the music that he loved, that he used to play for me in the car when we were driving on road trips, I realized that when you’re a writer, you don’t know quite why you write something until years later. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, she was also eager to reteam with her “country strong” collaborators jenno topping and randall poster, two people who feste said have believed in her the most over the course of her career. “So having them help me tell this story was just monumental. (Topping and Poster both produced “Heartland,” with Poster also serving as music supervisor, as he did on “Country Strong. It was being with someone that you knew had your back the entire time. ”) “When I’m having my darkest days about, I don’t know, me and what I create and my career, knowing that they believe in me has always been such a huge lift,” Feste said. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, if “heartland” sees misty feeling ill at ease in the very spaces that used to celebrate her talent, feste had the opposite experience. Six films into her directing career, she said “Heartland” let her approach her work in an entirely new way. And it felt good.

Diungkapkan bahwa “what was really valuable with this experience is that i felt completely comfortable saying, ‘i don’t know,’ and i don’t know if i’ve ever felt that way,” she said. It was only working with this group of filmmakers, Jenno and Randy and [production designer] Naomi [Shohan], some of my heads of production, that I knew that they saw my vulnerability not as a weakness, but as a strength. I was able to say, ‘I don’t know, what do you think?’ That’s where a very new form of collaboration happened that I haven’t experienced in my career, and with Jessica as well. “Certainly not with my first few films, feeling like as a woman, I had to know every answer from every head of department immediately. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, casting chastain was an easy call for feste. She wanted someone who could sing and who was admired in this space, but Chastain’s way of working and approach to on-set life gave Feste more to work with than she could have dreamed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i always want my films, especially when we’re shooting a movie that takes place in nashville, to feel authentic, and i knew jessica already had a huge buy-in from this audience. “And Jessica can sing, and that is another qualifier. But I think most of all, Jessica is one of the biggest champions of other women that I’ve ever met. The South, they love her from ‘George & Tammy,’” Feste said. Whenever I’m making any kind of movie with music, I want the actors to be able to sing their own material. ”.

It was freeing for Feste to say “I don’t know,” but Chastain also made it clear that she was there to support Feste’s vision and leadership.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “there were certain times on set where it would get a little loud or kind of disorderly, and people would be talking and having opinions, and no matter what, she’d be like, ‘shana, sorry, i couldn’t hear you,’ and it was like this just gentle reminder, ‘this is who is leading the ship right now for me,’” the filmmaker recalled. “It was done in the classiest, most polite way. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that approach turned the collaboration into more of a partnership. When Chastain had an idea, Feste was eager to listen. Even a decade ago, she said, that might not have been so easy for her.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “if i had been the director that i was 10 years ago, it would’ve scared me to death, because jessica is not afraid to come into a scene and say, ‘ok, wait, that might not be serving us. This wasn’t a scary experience. And to be able to relinquish control and admit when my idea wasn’t the best idea and she’s coming in with a stronger idea because she is Jessica Chastain? She has done the work. Let’s throw that idea out of the window. It was actually going to elevate the scene and make it work even better. She has made this character so rich. “As a director, I’m planning, and every shot is in my head, and I’ve done the work, and I’ve done the homework, and I’m the A student. What if we did this?,’” Feste said. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it was always the plan for feste’s stars to also sing their songs to add to the film’s deeper authenticity. “When I’m watching movies that feature performing artists, and there’s so much hype, and they’re playing this celebrated musical performer, and then they come on, and we hear them sing and we’re like, have they been re-voiced? It’s just kind of mediocre? You just kind of lose your authenticity. You lose the ownership of the movie,” she said.

Berdasarkan laporan, casting jennifer nettles was something of a no-brainer for feste, and so was actually directing the country superstar. “Most of the time I said, ‘Just speak to the audience like you are at the Opry, like you’ve done a thousand times. Make it your own. ’ She did so much heavy lifting for me. That is something that’s not in my repertoire of directing. “I didn’t know how to direct someone how to move on stage. I can direct someone talking about their divorce in a bedroom, but how to command a stage and move your body? That is something that she learned over 20 years of experience being a superstar,” she said. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so too did carter faith. Was Misty an Emmylou Harris? A Miranda Lambert? And who was young rising star Charlie Heart? Was she a Taylor Swift type? Poster had an easy answer: She sounds like this actual rising star, Carter Faith. In early discussions about the five characters in the film who are musical artists, Feste said she and Poster were constantly trying to figure out who they would sound like in the real world. And when it became clear that Faith was able to and interested in auditioning for the role? Serendipity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “she was like a breath of fresh air,” feste said. So much of her experience was exactly what the character was going through. ’ My heart exploded. Then I heard her story of how she was eating red beans and rice, crashing on couches, calling all of these places on Lower Broadway just to get an audition to be the performer at 10:00 AM on a Monday morning. So it was only the question of, are you brave enough to access all that trauma of how you got here? And she was absolutely, she said yes, and she trusted me, and it makes me emotional thinking about it because that’s an incredible trust to have. She is someone who really moved to Nashville the day she graduated from high school to make it. “I remember asking her, ‘Carter, what do you think you have in common with Charlie?’ And she said, ‘Well, we both have boy names. She was Charlie. It was the most non-Hollywood endearing response. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa faith also wrote the lyrics to the song that plays at the end of the film, which feste sees as “dialogue that i could never write. “Working with musical performances in film, it is so additive because it just takes the storytelling to another level. It’s beyond physical blocking. It’s beyond the dialogue. ” All the songs in the film and on its soundtrack, including the ones Feste simply imagined as titles first, like “Texas Land,” or that her stars like John Hawkes wrote or that Poster commissioned, add to the film’s incredible authentic feeling and sound. It tells story in this just purely emotional, raw, beautiful way,” she said.

Berdasarkan laporan, next up: in true feste fashion, she’s working on or thinking about a variety of other projects next, including the next chapter of the “dirty diana” story, which she first cooked up during lockdown, a tv series about a southern family, and her “dream project,” which is about texas bank robbers. I think that’s my bread and butter. Mostly, she said, “I really want to continue working in this space. I want to continue telling stories about messy, complicated, vulnerable Southern women. ”.
