#354. ’12 12 12′ Review: Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan’s Ticking-Clock Heist Thriller Runs on Broken Time

📅 13 Nov 2026

’12 12 12′ Review: Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan’s Ticking-Clock Heist Thriller Runs on Broken Time

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.indiewire.com/criticism/shows/12-12-12-review-apple-tv-series-heist-anthony-mackie-1235227284/

Diungkapkan bahwa every episode of “12 12 12” opens with the same explanation of its title: citing the fictitious law enforcement manual, “principles of crime, fbi research center, 4th edition,” anthony mackie explains, “a high asset robbery, professionally conceived, is 12 months in planning, 12 hours in execution. And then, we’re off to the races. A bank robber who’s not caught within 12 days is not caught at all. ” Then the screen splits horizontally to reveal images from the 12 months of preparation, the 12 hours of execution, and the 12 days when thief extraordinaire Paul Galvin (Jamie Dornan) does his best to elude Mackie’s obsessed FBI agent Jack Strickland. Related Stories ‘The Good Daughter’ Review: Rose Byrne Sizzles in Peacock’s Brutal Trauma-Drama About Crime-Solving Sisters ‘American Doctor’ and ‘You Can See Everything’ Lead 2027 Cinema Eye Honors Film Nominations.

Diungkapkan bahwa the heist genre, in theory, seems ripe for this kind of temporal manipulation. A game of wits between cops and criminals typically involves plenty of twists, many of which pull the rug out by flashing back to show where, when, and how it was placed so stealthily underfoot. Also working in “12 12 12’s” favor is the genre’s familiarity: There will be “getting the team together” montages, there will be unexpected hiccups in the days and hours during the robbery, there will be chest-thumping meetings between our confident cop and the equally confident con artist. Throw in the complex heist itself and the tense escape soon after, and there appear to be enough recognizable pieces that jumbling them up shouldn’t prove too confusing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and “12 12 12” isn’t confusing. Taking a serpentine route through well-trodden territory does more to undermine our enjoyment of an otherwise well-mounted chase than it does to liven things up. It is, however, convoluted. They’re exciting in conception (when master thieves can wow us with their slick plans), they’re exciting to see carried out (when the shit hits the fan and even the most astute architects have to think on their feet), and they’re exciting to get away with (when safety is within reach, but it could be snatched away at any moment). Heists are inherently exciting. Anticipation, suspense, and anxiety work to form a natural arc, and disrupting that arc over and over, every hour for eight hours, in service of a few extra twists — and to extend what’s obviously a movie-length story across eight hours — simply isn’t worth it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on that note, let me get this minor but essential point out of the way now, quickly and clearly: jamie dornan needs more weird roles, not more conventional ones. We saw what he can do in “Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar” (a modern comedy classic). (Remember the bee movie?! No, not that bee movie — the other one. Let the man cook — or sing or dance or all three at once! He can do it! Honestly, I believe he can do anything. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa anyway, here his character’s only unique attribute is his brilliant… planning. Caught in a bind with his dumbass brother (Jack Kesy, doing his best Travis Kelce impression), Bobby lays it out in aptly blunt terms: “Paul, you’re the fucking plan guy, so plan me a plan. He’s got a mind for details, and he uses it to map out every possible contingency before embarking on his elaborate heists. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but the only plans paul wants to make these days are for his family: he’s happy working on fishing boats off the coast of france and coming home to his wife, severine (agathe rousselle), in their little apartment above a bar. He’s bonded with his father-in-law, Serge (José Garcia), who’s the Marxist papa Paul never had, and he’s got a kid on the way.

Sebagaimana diketahui, unfortunately, bobby can’t stop being bobby and winds up indebted to the wrong people; people who don’t just want their money back, but who want more money to make up for the inconvenience. And since Bobby already owes more money than either brother could ever pay back, Paul has to take on one last job to free his brother — and himself — from their lives of crime.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, too bad that puts him back on jack’s radar or, i should say, squarely on jack’s radar, since jack is nursing a (secret) grudge against paul from years earlier. He wants revenge, he wants “respect,” he wants to win — “12 12 12” throws out a number of motivations for Jack early on that clearly don’t paint the full picture. Ever since, he’s been obsessed with catching the one criminal who’s eluded his grasp. They’re placeholder reasons until the show deems it time to dig into what’s really driving him to move to Zurich, hole up in a shitty police station, and wait for Paul to try to steal something.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mackie, who’s reunited with his “falcon and the winter soldier” director kari skogland, gives great determined face, and dornan is the softest, sweetest guy on the fbi’s most-wanted list. (He doesn’t want to steal, but now that he must, he’s going to do it the right way. Thankfully, co-creators Dudi Appleton and Jim Keeble don’t ask their lead characters to betray their core identities amid all the twists and turns, shading Jack as more of an antagonist (all-consumed and, thus, single-minded to a fault) and Paul as more of the protagonist. ) That helps keep our rooting interests in line, which goes a long way toward a satisfying emotional payoff, even when the momentum ebbs and flows with every flash-forward, -back, and -sideways.

Diungkapkan bahwa with slick locations and clever-enough problem-solving, “12 12 12” should satisfy die-hard heist fans (but not “die hard’s” heist fans). It just takes a circuitous route to scratching that itch, and that’s almost as aggravating as not scratching it at all.

Berdasarkan laporan, “12 12 12” premieres friday, november 13 on apple tv with two episodes. New episodes will be released weekly through the finale (Episode 8) on December 25.

#363. Johnny Depp's Ebenezer Features One Character Most Adaptations Usually Cut

📅 13 Nov 2026

Johnny Depp's Ebenezer Features One Character Most Adaptations Usually Cut

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2316683/johnny-depp-ebenezer-character-adaptations-cut-scrooge-sister/

Berdasarkan laporan, at this point in the life of charles dickens' 1843 novella "a christmas carol," so many stage and screen adaptations have been produced that the process of boiling the story down to its core elements has turned them into veritable tropes unto themselves. This aspect was being parodied as long ago as 1988's "Scrooged," which utilized an adaptation-within-an-adaptation as a bit of meta satire, as well as a commentary on how rote adapting Dickens' tale had become. Everything from a Victorian London setting to the line "God bless us, everyone" became not just quintessential to a new adaptation, but necessary, in much the same manner as the umpteenth cover of a popular song carries its own expectations. In a similar fashion to the elements which began to be regarded as a must-include, there were some other elements seen in Dickens' novella which got treated as unnecessary, and thus became more and more overlooked.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the most notable of these latter elements is the presence of a sister character for ebenezer scrooge. Yet Fan or her equivalent tends to be missing or altered in most modern adaptations. It would be erroneous to say that the sister is always cut from "A Christmas Carol" adaptations. This month's "Ebenezer," then, holds the honor of reinstating a sister character close to Dickens' Fan after a lengthy absence. After all, Fan Scrooge (as played by Carol Marsh) appears in one of the most revered film versions of the story, Brian Desmond Hurst's "A Christmas Carol" from 1951 starring Alistair Sim. She's nowhere in "Scrooged" or "The Muppet Christmas Carol," and she's heavily changed in the 2019 BBC miniseries starring Guy Pearce. While this is admirable, the reason for it doing so is due to the film's awkward revisionist take on Scrooge, as played by Johnny Depp.

Diungkapkan bahwa in "ebenezer" as in "a christmas carol," scrooge is reunited with his sister during his trip through his earlier years, courtesy of the ghost of christmas past (andrea riseborough). As in Dickens' novella, the sister is a fairly beatific figure, a protector of the bullied (and, it's heavily implied, abused by their father) Scrooge. In the film, screenwriter Nathaniel Halpern has renamed the sister from Fan to Molly (for what reason, only he knows), played by Rose Williams.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on the one hand, one wonders why so many adaptations mess around with the character, considering how important she is to scrooge's nephew, fred (sam claflin). She's literally his mother, and the idea of Scrooge shunning Fred due to his discomfort over the untimely death of his beloved sister is a good source of dramatic tension.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yet on the other hand, it's likely that most adaptations either reconfigure or leave the sister out because her presence exists to humanize scrooge in a way that some adaptations would rather not deal with. The sister and her fleshing out of Scrooge's origin story, as it were, forces the character to be more nuanced. Of course, most intelligent audience members should be able to understand that a young victim turned adult monster doesn't mean his misdeeds are automatically forgiven, yet those who think of "A Christmas Carol" primarily as a story for young children might.

Berdasarkan laporan, in any case, "ebenezer" corrects this error too far the other way, adding to it some other odd changes which make scrooge a little too sympathetic. At least director Ti West and company don't let him completely off the hook, either, but it's too bad that the sister is re-included in the film for little more reason than as a character witness.

"Avengers: Doomsday" is almost upon us, but the titular roster looks a lot different in 2026 than it did when "The Avengers" debuted back in 2012. 's Tony Stark/Iron Man, and Jeremy Renner's Clint Barton/Hawkeye. That means the only original member in "Doomsday" will be Thor, and if he's fully welcomed back into the fold, Steve Rogers.

#370. 7 Sci-Fi Shows Fans Either Love Or Hate

📅 13 Nov 2026

7 Sci-Fi Shows Fans Either Love Or Hate

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/sci-fi-shows-fans-love-or-hate/

Berdasarkan laporan, sci-fi tv shows are notoriously difficult to get right. The idea of a universally beloved science fiction series is basically a myth. Even the most celebrated sci-fi shows have detractors who are every bit as vocal as their supporters. The genre’s fandom can be fickle, and even the grandest ideas or most impressive visual spectacle cannot guarantee a series will succeed. However, some sci-fi shows take that divide to another level, earning reputations as timeless masterpieces and embarrassing low points in almost the same breath.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these aren’t shows that are so bad they become entertaining, either. When it gets interesting is with the shows that have a strong premise and something substantial to offer, whether that’s inventive storytelling, memorable characters, or a fresh approach to an established universe. It’s understandable when a deliberately B-Movie-style sci-fi series splits the genre’s fandom down the middle. Their most controversial qualities are often precisely what their admirers treasure, making their divisive nature almost as fascinating as the sci-fi stories they tell.

Berdasarkan laporan, few shows demand such an immediate leap of faith as the oa. Its story begins with Prairie Johnson (Brit Marling), a previously blind woman who returns after disappearing for seven years, now able to see. The whole thing is incredibly surreal both conceptually and visually, and for The OA’s fans, the rejection of conventional storytelling is the attraction. What follows combines near-death experiences, alternate dimensions, and characters that can supposedly transcend ordinary reality. The series treats belief and human connection with an earnestness that makes its strangest developments feel emotionally meaningful, even when their mechanics can’t really be explained.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, that prioritizing of emotional sincerity makes the oa difficult viewing for anyone who cannot accept its central concepts and premise. The dialogue sometimes tries a little too hard to be profound, and its mysteries require a lot of patience before offering anything resembling clarity. Where fans see a sci-fi show brave enough to let viewers have their own interpretation of what’s happening, skeptics see The OA as a series that mistakes obscurity for depth.

Berdasarkan laporan, continuing the story of a celebrated graphic novel as a tv show was always going to provoke disagreement, especially when that graphic novel is alan moore’s watchmen. HBO’s series moves the action to an alternate 2019, where masked police officers confront a white supremacist organization in Tulsa. Detective Angela Abar (Regina King) becomes the center of a mystery connecting racial violence and the concealed history of costumed heroes, all of which is underpinned by an exploration of inherited trauma. Fans praised the show for finding fresh relevance in its source material, but many viewers had a much less positive response.

Sebagaimana diketahui, many viewers openly disliked the heavy emphasis hbo’s watchmen placed on american racism, while others find the treatment of legacy characters like dr. Few critical voices found flaws in the show as a TV series. The disagreement ultimately concerns what a continuation owes its predecessor. Manhattan and Ozymandius completely missed the point of Alan Moore’s original story. Fans loved the way HBO’s Watchmen used the world of the graphic novel to explore contemporary social anxieties, while those who loved the source material completely rejected the way it used the world of Watchmen as a vehicle to make a political statement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in theory, an alien invasion should lead to a high-octane, action-packed sci-fi story. Following people across different countries as extraterrestrial forces arrive, the series emphasizes personal grief, and the confusion of experiencing a catastrophe without understanding its scale rather than grand spectacle. Apple TV’s Invasion, however, takes a deliberately different approach, and it turned pit to be a polarizing one. The threat of the invasion still feels enormous, but it’s due to the characters' responses to what’s going on rather than any kind of grand explosive display of advanced alien technology. Some people loved this unique approach to an alien invasion narrative, but others very much didn’t.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for invasion’s detractors, the slow-burn of the unfolding catastrophe felt like a stalled narrative. The focus on grounded moments like domestic arguments or panic attacks occupied a lot of narrative space without doing much to make the characters more compelling. The show’s perspective is an interesting idea, but an interesting idea doesn’t make up for bad pacing. Those invested in its atmosphere appreciate living through uncertainty alongside the characters experience it, but viewers waiting for meaningful developments feel that Invasion keeps postponing the story its premise promised.

Berdasarkan laporan, for some fans, star trek: discovery brought urgency and emotional openness to a franchise that needed to evolve. Discovery as they navigate a radically unfamiliar future. Its admirers praise its cinematic presentation, inclusive ensemble cast, and insistence that compassion remains meaningful under extreme pressure. Centering on Michael Burnham (Sonequa Martin-Green), it follows the crew of the U. S. S. Rather than presenting optimism as an uncomplicated starting point like many Star Trek shows, Discovery frequently makes its characters struggle toward it, giving their commitment to cooperation a personal intensity that resonates strongly with its audience.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this intensity is exactly why star trek: discovery is perhaps the most polarizing star trek show so far. Burnham’s repeated importance to enormous crises also makes the wider universe feel unusually dependent on a single character, a trait that feels much closer to Star Wars than it does Trek. Its season-long emergencies leave less room for exploratory adventures-of-the-week, while leaning into emotional speeches often interrupts situations that demand immediate action. Essentially, Discovery created intense debates around what a Star Trek series should prioritize, and the discussion still rages on two years after it concluded.

Diungkapkan bahwa the appeal of rick & morty extends beyond increasingly elaborate sci-fi jokes. It’s a series that moves from grotesque sic-if flavored slapstick to existential despair with remarkable speed. The adventures of its central duo use grand concepts like multiversal travel as ways to explore deep psychological problems, such as if alternate realities make family members replaceable or if scientific genius justifies rejecting emotional attachment. Rick & Morty fans see this versatility as its greatest strength. It’s capable of mocking sci-fi’s absurdity while also finding genuine emotional depth in the implications of the genre’s grandest concepts.

Berdasarkan laporan, the problem for those on the other side of the fence is that rick & morty is seen as a series that insists upon itself. For those that hate it, the belching, gore, sexual jokes, and gratuitousness are the series true identity, and capping off an episode with a moment or two of philosophical insight doesn’t change this. Not only that, but the show’s nihilistic approach to narrative consequences makes it impossible to ever truly care about Rick, Morty, or any other character, according to some. Ultimately, Rick & Morty is a show filled with emotional contradictions, and this seems central to both its appeal and the frustration it inspires.

Diungkapkan bahwa set roughly a century before the phantom menace, the acolyte had an unusually promising opportunity to explore a relatively untouched period in the star wars timeline. Fans of The Acolyte immediately praised both the distance from the Skywalker saga and the Disney+ Star Wars show’s willingness to question the Jedi’s confidence in their own judgment. An investigation into attacks on Jedi gradually exposes buried wrongdoing and, eventually, some major flaws in the order’s central philosophy. However, an intriguing premise does not automatically produce a great sci-fi TV show.

Sebagaimana diketahui, even beyond those who didn’t appreciate the jedi being portrayed at their most fallible, plenty of people hated the acolyte for what they viewed as awkward dialogue, uneven pacing, and difficult-to-understand character decisions. For The Acolyte’s admirers, its storytelling flaws are easy to look past thanks to it being a worthwhile expansion of the franchise’s moral tapestry. There were plenty of complaints that had nothing to do with the show’s reframing of Jedi history. For others, the show is a flawed execution of ideas that are far less complex than they claim to be, leaving a potentially compelling mystery sidelined by an attempt to unnecessarily upend Star Wars canon.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while the story that followed became incredibly divisive, it's almost universally agreed that lost’s central premise of plane crash survivors awakening on an island filled with impossible phenomena is exceptionally solid. Lost turns its setup into an expansive mystery box drama about damaged people confronting circumstances they cannot explain. Flashbacks give seemingly straightforward conflicts unexpected emotional weight, while the island’s secrets make almost every discovery feel significant. It’s what the show does with that idea that makes it one of the most polarizing sci-fi shows ever made. For the first few seasons, this was enough. However, as Lost went on, the cracks in viewer responses started to show.

Berdasarkan laporan, in many ways, lost created this problem for itself by inviting viewers to scrutinize every detail. Over a decade after it concluded, that division remains. Those that loved the show were happy with how the dots joined up. It created expectations about how those details would eventually connect. For some viewers, Lost is one of the greatest sci-fi shows ever made. Those that didn’t either hate the end result, or simply grew sick of the constant drip-feed of mysteries with comparatively few tangible answers. The finale of Lost crystallized that disagreement by prioritizing emotional reunion over clearly explaining what the island is and how it worked. For others, it’s a reason to be mad at ABC for hours of viewing they’re never going to get back.

#371. 5 Near-Perfect Fantasy Books, Recommended by Brandon Sanderson

Sebagaimana diketahui, brandon sanderson is one of the most popular authors in the fantasy genre right now, yet he never misses a chance to pay his success forward. His story of single-minded focus on becoming a professional author is inspiring to many readers, and he often encourages aspiring young writers to read as much as possible. Sanderson has made headlines for steering the publishing industry itself and advocating for other writers along the way. However, Sanderson qualifies all of his book recommendations with the caveat that not every book will resonate with every reader. He encourages fans to read widely and seek out what interests them most.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that said, fans are often interested in what their favorite authors are inspired by, and sanderson has not been stingy about sharing. Berdasarkan laporan, in his post, sanderson recommends the works of tad williams in general, but williams is best known for his series memory, sorrow, & thorn. R. This series was a massive influence on George R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire, and likely many others. Sebagaimana diketahui, sanderson warns that williams' writing can be "very long-winded," adding that he personally likes this style, but it might put others off in the early chapters. The series follows a young man named Simon thrust into an apocalyptic struggle against ancient magical forces. He also listed Williams among the "clean" authors on his list, though there are some extremely dark themes in Memory, Sorrow, and Thorn. Sebagaimana diketahui, sanderson has mentioned dragonsbane by barbara hambly many times in posts, interviews, and lectures, saying it's one of the main reasons he became interested in fantasy. He also used it as an example of following your own interests as a reader, pointing out that no one would have predicted a teenage boy would be interested the esoteric adventures of a middle-aged woman. Years after its publication, Hambly began writing sequels to Dragonsbane, with new installments still coming out today.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the story is about a witch named jenny waynest who lives a harsh, relatively isolated life in the northlands along with the lord john aversin. Not only is the dragon Morkeleb more powerful than they expected, but the king is under the influence of another witch who did not want Jenny to make the journey. They are asked to come south to help fend of an ancient, powerful dragon that is encroaching on the more populous city. They do so in exchange for aid for their Northlands, but they find the situation in the south more complicated than they expected. The book was lauded by fiction readers when it was published in 1985, and Sanderson's recommendation has brought it back into the conversation in recent years.

Berdasarkan laporan, again, sanderson recommends "anything by daniel abraham under any of his various pen names," but the dagger and the coin series is a great place to start. A. Corey. It's one of the most popular series Abraham has published under his own name, though he is best known to many fans for co-writing The Expanse series under the pen name James S. The name refers to both Abraham and Ty Franck, who are currently using the Corey moniker once again for a sci-fi series called The Captive's War.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the dagger and the coin consists of five books published from 2011 to 2016. It's an epic fantasy series with a broad scope and many point of view characters, often earning it comparisons to A Song of Ice and Fire. Abraham is a friend and frequent collaborator of Martin, so this should come as no surprise. The series is named for two very different forces that can both lead to calamity for humanity — the dagger representing violence and war, and the coin representing economic instability.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the hundred thousand kingdoms is the first book in n. In those books, magic-users called Orogenes have the ability to control seismic energy, and through that affect the climate indirectly. Both of Jemisin's trilogies are beautifully written and incredibly compelling, as are her stand-alone novels. K. Jemisin employs hard magic systems in her writing much like Sanderson, though the comparison is more often made with Jemisin's next series, The Broken Earth Trilogy. Jemisin's The Inheritance Trilogy, followed by The Broken Kingdoms and The Kingdom of the Gods. The series is set in a unique fantasy world drawing inspiration from many cultures and regions — not just medieval Europe. They are definitely worth checking out for Sanderson fans — or any fantasy fans for that matter.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, finally, sanderson recommends "anything by robin hobb, but particularly the fitz books," referring to hobb's 16-book series the realm of the elderlings. It's a spectacular case of grounded, character-driven stories somehow building to an epic, fantastical saga. This series is broken up into five parts, three of which follow the character Fitzchivalry Farseer and are written in the first person. The series has a unique focus on magical ecology, leading to some truly unique takes on fantasy tropes like dragons and prophecies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sanderson's recommendations are all excellent, especially when taken alongside his encouragement to explore the genre for yourself. It's a great time to be a fantasy fan right now, and it's great to see authors like Sanderson encouraging their readers to branch out. All of the books mentioned here are available now in print, digital, and audiobook formats.

Diungkapkan bahwa overwatch players who wanted a new support hero were less excited to learn that they weren't getting the cool omnic detective they were promised. Some called it a "bait and switch. " Overwatch currently has 23 damage heroes. Hudson will be the 24th.

Berdasarkan laporan, on friday, keller responded to backlash about hudson's place on the overwatch roster, offering more context on the decision to "help players understand it, even as some of them are disappointed. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, "when we started work on the detective, he was a support," keller said in a thread on x. "But as time went on and the kit continued development we realized that it wasn’t working. Once we tested Hudson as a DPS, the turn around in our feelings for him was instantaneous and dramatic.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this decision ultimately wasn't whether we release a dps or a support hero, it was whether we release a great character or one we didn't believe in. Sebagaimana diketahui, the "one mile" movies are directed by adam davidson, who has a prolific career stretching back to the late-'80s when he made his directorial debut with the short "the lunch date. Diungkapkan bahwa per flixpatrol, not only have both chapters been in the paramount+ charts for over a month, until november 13, 2026, "chapter one" was sitting at the very top of the u. movie charts, with "Chapter Two" occupying the second spot. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as "doctor who" fans (aka whovians) are no doubt aware, the show is in a bit of a bind. The character, you see, is a time-traveling alien known as a Time Lord, and when they die, they're able to regenerate into a new person. Since its debut way back in 1963, the series has sustained itself with a clever sci-fi concept that has allowed multiple actors to canonically play the title role of the Doctor. Each time the Doctor regenerates, their personality changes a bit, although they still have the same memories, intellect, and enthusiasm.

Sebagaimana diketahui, unfortunately, after running for so long, "doctor who" has developed a bad habit of falling back on stale tropes. A Whovian friend of mine has agreed that "Doctor Who" is in a bad place right now, and the franchise's future is uncertain in the wake of Disney ending its partnership with the show due to its relatively low viewership. As my friend put it, the series is, indeed, in a "tepid" place, and no one knows where it will go moving forward.

Berdasarkan laporan, peter capaldi, however, has some suggestions. The actor, who played the Twelfth Doctor from 2014 to 2017, shared his ideas during his recent appearance on the "Half the Picture" podcast, explaining that he thinks the show needs to get back to basics. He added that it would do well to reorient itself by returning to its lower budgeted origins and tapping back into the shoddy charms of its earliest days.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the same interview, peter capaldi clarified that he is fine with no longer being associated with "doctor who," as there are other ventures he would like to pursue. "Doctor Who," he noted, is the kind of show that takes over your life, adding, "You can't do it [. ] as a part-time role. " When it comes to the property's future, though, Capaldi is uncertain, stating:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "what it's got to be, i don't know. That's what I grew up with. I was thinking about this [. ' I mean, 'Doctor Who' has always had ambition, it's just that budgets haven't always met that. Because my love for the show was the old show. Let's make it black-and-white with very wobbly sets. Or with less ambition. And that's not going to work. ] I don't know what people want from it. Let's make more cheaply. I can't come in and say 'Let's set it in the '60s. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, capaldi then mused out loud if audiences might want "david and kylie. Or maybe they're more interested in previous "Doctor Who" stars like Christopher Eccleston or Jodie Whitaker. " He was, of course, referring to David Tennant's highly popular iteration of the Doctor appearing with a character played by Kylie Minogue on "Doctor Who" in the 2007 Christmas special "Voyage of the Damned" (which brought in an impressive number of viewers). Basically, Capaldi is very unsure what fans really want out of the series.

Sebagaimana diketahui, all he can say is that he enjoys "doctor who" the best when it experiences what he calls a "ripple" from the old show. Not a reused monster, necessarily, but a specific tone that sometimes breaks through. Something humble and old-fashioned.

Sebagaimana diketahui, although "doctor who" is a time-travel series that involves aliens, monsters, major historical figures, and ineffable, universe-ending technologies, peter capaldi feels that it's actually a "small" show. It's about a small group of characters and their time-traveling TARDIS, which looks like a police box that, via advanced technology, is larger on the inside than on the outside. Capaldi added that if the series could focus on those basics, it could sing once again, explaining:.

Diungkapkan bahwa "it's the doctor and the assistant-slash-assistants in the tardis. And like in 'The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe,' they step out the door to this drama. Quite contained. Magical, strange, weird, sad. It's that central core of that small group of people with the Doctor at the center of it. And those dramas change shape, and they've got monsters in them. Kind of balming. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa i have personally watched enough of the show to know that most of the best "doctor who" episodes embody what capaldi talked about. The problem, then, is that many of the series' seasonal storylines climax with some sort of supervillain threatening to destroy the universe, unwrite history, or commit some other kind of massive sci-fi cataclysm. And if those types of cataclysms are regularly happening, then it's no surprise that fans are experiencing a sense of fatigue (or that the show's creatives may be running low on ideas).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, time will tell if the minds currently behind "doctor who" take capaldi's advice and scale the series back into a cheaper, more humble form. It certainly wouldn't hurt, what with the series being adrift following its short-lived Disney era and the planned 2026 Christmas special being canceled. Capaldi might just be onto something.

#386. Johnny Depp’s ‘Ebenezer’ Makes a Weak Case for His Post-Trial Comeback

📅 13 Nov 2026

Johnny Depp’s ‘Ebenezer’ Makes a Weak Case for His Post-Trial Comeback

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/ebenezer-johnny-depp-comeback

Sebagaimana diketahui, for weeks, los angeles has been plastered with posters of a malevolent-looking man in a top hat and gray sideburns. It always takes me a few minutes to process that this elderly curmudgeon is Johnny Depp, doing his Hollywood walk of shame in Ebenezer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it’s good to be back,” depp gurgles in the movie’s trailer. He’s either reveling in his return from infamy or trolling the audience, depending on your point of view.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i adored johnny depp back in his edward scissorhands/gilbert grape/ed wood heyday; he probably would’ve been my hall pass if i’d known about the concept back then. Now, though, it feels as if the once chiseled-cheeked heartthrob has found a character that suits him: a monstrous figure seeking redemption.

#393. Mississippi Goddam: Scott Colom Is the Answer to Anyone Who Looked Down on the South

📅 13 Nov 2026

Mississippi Goddam: Scott Colom Is the Answer to Anyone Who Looked Down on the South

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/scott-colom-mississippi-essay

Berdasarkan laporan, “mississippi is not who you think we are. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa this is what an older black woman said to ms now’s nnamdi egwuonwu as he interviewed scott colom supporters on the tougaloo college campus thursday night. The crowd was waiting for Colom to speak after his historic victory, becoming the first Black Mississippian elected to statewide office since Reconstruction, and its first Democratic senator in nearly a half century. The woman did not give her name, but her simple statement has tattooed itself inside my brain.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “to understand the world, you must first understand a place like mississippi” is a more famous cautionary quip that scratches at the same sentiment. If you’ve known anyone from Mississippi, you’ve probably heard it. Everyone cites William Faulkner, even though nobody has definitively sourced it. But as the world looks with fresh eyes on my home state, the wisdom checks out.

Berdasarkan laporan, onlookers, including longtime national political strategists, seem surprised by colom’s win. Mississippians are not. The extremes of the moral universe have always been duking it out down there, which makes Mississippi not strange or anomalous, but illustrative.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there’s no avoiding the facts: human beings have committed the most brutal violence imaginable against their fellow humans in mississippi, as a matter of law and legacy. #394. Johnny Depp's Ebenezer Makes An Alarming Change To The Story Of A Christmas Carol

📅 13 Nov 2026

Johnny Depp's Ebenezer Makes An Alarming Change To The Story Of A Christmas Carol

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2315819/johnny-depp-ebenezer-a-christmas-carol-story-change/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when the ads and pre-release buzz articles began running for "ebenezer," the new film directed by ti west and starring johnny depp as scrooge, the campaign promised that the movie would present charles dickens' "a christmas carol" as you'd never seen it before. The movie liberally copy-and-pastes whole swathes of Dickens' text into the script, with writer Nathaniel Halpern even bothering to include the novella's separation into five staves. Yet, now that the film has released and folks (including yours truly) have screened it, it turns out "Ebenezer" is unsurprisingly more or less the same "A Christmas Carol" we all know well. However, it seems there's some larger artistic liberty wiggle room in that "more or less the same" than might appear at first glance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when west spoke to entertainment weekly back in august, he detailed what made depp's ebenezer different than previous adaptations. Amidst talking up things like Depp's "musicality" as a performer, West also explained how his film would present Scrooge in a more both sides-y manner: "As [Depp's] Scrooge cuts someone down verbally or as he makes a financial point or withdraws, you do understand why he's doing it. " That offhand mention of "a financial point" baffled many of us when we first read it, as it certainly did sound like a deviation from Dickens.

Diungkapkan bahwa was this scrooge going to be portrayed as a genius businessman? instead, the changes "ebenezer" makes to scrooge and dickens' story are of a smaller nature. They involve portraying a couple small supporting characters as outright villains, thereby giving Scrooge a justification for his misanthropy. The changes may be merely tweaks, yet their larger implications are alarming, especially for a film which doesn't feel able to support them.

Diungkapkan bahwa for the most part, "ebenezer" is a faithful adaptation of "a christmas carol. Marley goes to get some tea while Scrooge observes a beggar outside his window. " The largest addition comes in the form of a prologue in which we see Scrooge and his partner, Jacob Marley (Ian McKellen), on their last day together. At the same moment the beggar reveals himself to Scrooge as a fraud conning people out of their donations, Marley drops dead, equating the con artist's crime with harm done to a true earner in Scrooge's mind. That Marley (and Scrooge) are just as heartless and dishonest is something the film hopes Dickens' work gets across, as they don't go out of their way to underline it to support their addition.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this problem is compounded twice. Once is when it's revealed that Scrooge's old benevolent boss Fezziwig was murdered by a street beggar, further teaching Scrooge that charity can be met with violence. Next is when the Ghost of Christmas Future shows Scrooge the vultures who've come to sully his legacy after his death, which adds the wrinkle that the two men who sought a donation for the poor at the beginning of the film are actually also embezzlers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what's more, they're in league with a man who's plotting with the embezzlers to steal scrooge's nephew fred's inheritance with the production of a forged will. The alarming quality about these inclusions lies in how they seem to give Scrooge more moral justification for his odious behavior that he doesn't need. It's a bizarrely tone-deaf addition for a story that's ultimately meant to be about the virtues of charity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ultimately (and thankfully), these additions do not derail "ebenezer," for the heart of charles dickens' story and his themes remains intact. Although it's tempting to point fingers at the Skydance corporation for the new ideas, it isn't the changes themselves that are the problem. "Ebenezer" is indeed partially constructed to emphasize the horror in Dickens' tale: the three Christmas ghosts are more ghastly and doomed than they typically are. After all, Ti West comes from a background of indie horror films, many of which utilize thorny, morally ambiguous characterizations and themes as their stock in trade. In the more horror-centric version of "A Christmas Carol" the movie seems to want to be, a somewhat justified Scrooge would be a fascinating layer for an actor to play, as it creates a new obstacle for the character to overcome on his journey to selflessness.

Sebagaimana diketahui, alas, "ebenezer" is the johnny depp show, and for several reasons, depp is not up to the task. Instead, "Ebenezer" and Depp are too preoccupied with trying to be as likable as possible, which means that his Scrooge rarely gets nasty. He comes off more like an irritable jerk than a man who's nearly lost his soul, so whatever compelling shadings the changes to the story could've presented never materialize. While it's arguable that he may not be able to tackle such material at all, it seems like he's not even interested in trying in the first place. On paper, the possibilities presented by "Ebenezer" range from exciting to alarming. Yet we needn't fret too much, since the finished film plays things so safely that it's hard to get riled up about it one way or the other.

#396. 3 Best Sci-Fi Books To Read This Weekend (November 14-15)

📅 13 Nov 2026

3 Best Sci-Fi Books To Read This Weekend (November 14-15)

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/best-sci-fi-books-read-this-weekend-november-14/

Sebagaimana diketahui, science fiction is among the most popular genres around, and for good reason. Rich in worldbuilding and dealing with themes of oppression, ambition, liberation, and the advancement of the human race, sci-fi is an enduring part of most media, but it's especially prominent in literature. Ever since Mary Shelley's foundational classic, Frankenstein, came out, the genre has kept growing until it became the juggernaut it is today.

Sebagaimana diketahui, today, sci-fi is incredibly prolific, and you can find at least one book about every single possible subgenre, tackling every possible angle. If you're in the mood for a riveting sci-fi book to read this weekend, then look no further than the ones on this list. One of these you can probably start and finish over the weekend, and the others might take a bit longer. However, they're all incredible choices for you to tackle come Saturday morning.

Berdasarkan laporan, you might know this title more for emma stone's oscar-winning 2023 adaptation, but the original poor things is just as quirky, subversive, and unforgettable — it's also rather different. D. Like the movie, Poor Things: Episodes from the Early Life of Archibald McCandless M. , Scottish Public Health Officer is a spin on Frankenstein focusing on Bella Baxter, a woman brought back to life with the brain of a baby in Victorian Glasgow.

Sebagaimana diketahui, like the movie, the book is wholly original, tracking bella's growth from an inexperienced, childlike girl into a liberated and knowledgeable young woman who learns, through experience, how to relate to and challenge the world's conventions. Gray's interest is entirely in offering a daring, postmodern dissection of Victorian society, particularly taking issue with the time's outdated social and sexual conventions. Most brilliant is the film's ending, in which letters from Bella herself put into question McCandless' retelling of her life, claiming she is neither the result of an experiment nor the idealized version that he depicts. It's one final, brilliant subversion of a well-known story that completely recontextualizes everything you just read.

Diungkapkan bahwa now we move on to one of the most critically acclaimed sci-fi books of the 2000s. A woman named Abigail Gentin has split herself into thousands of male and female clones known as shatterlings. House of Suns is set six million years into the future, as humanity has spread across the Milky Way. Two of them fall in love and arrive late to a family reunion, only to discover their fellow clones have been attacked by a mysterious force set on eradicating them.

Berdasarkan laporan, house of suns is among the most original, daring, and impactful explorations of identity in modern fiction. The result is one of the best sci-fi books of the 21st century, a remarkable and profound exercise in sci-fi that asks many intriguing questions without ever forgetting to deliver a compelling mystery. The premise is incredibly creative from the get-go, but the book's greatest strength is how it tackles issues of individuality within the context of a sprawling galaxy. How does one life matter in the grand context of the universe? Author Alastair Reynolds shoots for the stars here (pun intended). It's a bit under 500 pages, so you can comfortably end this one by Friday if you begin on Saturday morning.

Diungkapkan bahwa lastly, let's finish with one of the most popular and beloved sci-fi books of the 2010s. Andy Weir's best-selling juggernaut The Martian tells the story of Mark Watney, a botanist and engineer who becomes stranded on Mars after he's presumed dead. Left alone, and with only his wit and experience as allies, Watney has to, in his words, "science the s—t out of this. " Meanwhile, his crew on Earth works tirelessly to bring him home.

Berdasarkan laporan, weir creates genuine literary magic here. Watney's journey could become incredibly didactic, especially as he invests considerable time in his scientific process, using actual protocols and terms to survive. Yet, the author injects so much wit and personality into the writing that it practically comes alive before you. Watney is one of the best protagonists of the 21st century: ingenious, relatable, and remarkably human, endlessly optimistic despite being in a situation where so many others would've surrendered to despondency. It's no surprise that the book has become a true pop culture landmark, reviving mainstream interest in science fiction and launching Weir's career as one of the genre's best writers today.

On Monday, two maintenance workers initially found a heavy black garbage bag “covered in flies” with what they suspected were human remains inside near the dumpster area of the Pacifico Apartments, resulting in a 911 call, according to the affidavit.

Orlando police arrived and initially saw a man’s arm, which was wrapped in a blue sheet, inside the bag, the affidavit states.

The man identified as Martinez, 32, “was tied with an orange extension cord and wrapped in 3 black trash bags and a dark blue laundry bag,” an officer wrote in the affidavit.

An autopsy revealed he had “laceration to his neck as well as puncture wounds on his left side, lacerations on his left palm, and lacerations on the left side of his face,” the affidavit states.

Detectives searched the trash compactor that was near Martinez’s body and found several items with suspected blood, including a black sandal, a piece of mail, a broken knife, towels and blankets, according to police.

The investigation led officers to execute a search warrant at Hernandez’s apartment, where suspected blood was found throughout the residence, which appeared to have been recently cleaned, the affidavit states.

While there, a 21-year-old woman approached detectives and revealed her mother had been babysitting Hernandez’s two children — a 3-year-old daughter and a 1-year-old son — since Saturday, when the alleged killing occurred.

She said on Monday, the girl cried out saying, “‘Mama cut papa’ and made hand gestures mimicking a slicing motion along her arms, stomach, and neck,” the affidavit states.

Hernandez’s daughter also mentioned “blood” and “trash” to the babysitter, according to the filing.

Diungkapkan bahwa hernandez, who had bruising on her arm, was detained and told officers she had been involved in a physical altercation with martinez, whom she described as her husband but noted they’re not legally married, on saturday, the affidavit states. She accused him of choking her while holding a long knife.

At some point, she said she took the knife from him and demonstrated a “slashing motion,” according to the filing.

“Hernandez advised that she did not contact law enforcement due to fear; however, she later placed two calls to 911 in hopes that someone would find the decedent at the dumpster,” the affidavit states.

She allegedly also admitted to placing Martinez’s body in trash bags and leaving it near the dumpster.

“Statements made by the couple’s young child referencing her mother cutting someone, along with the subsequent bruising on Hernandez’s arm, provide additional context surrounding the events preceding the decedent’s death,” the officer wrote in the affidavit.

Hernandez’s public defender didn’t immediately return a request for comment from Us on Friday, November 13.

Hernandez is due in court for a hearing set for November 17, records show.

#398. How To Rob A Bank Director David Leitch Reveals His Favorite Scene In The Movie [Exclusive]

Diungkapkan bahwa warning: this article contains light spoilers for "how to rob a bank. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, david leitch doesn't make things easy, and that's entirely by design. The unconventional, genre-redefining heist flick almost immediately makes a choice to embrace its own way of doing things — in this case, using a content creator aesthetic as star Nicholas Hoult's main protagonist Ryan (aka The Wolf) and his criminal crew go viral with their DIY social media channel. His latest, "How to Rob a Bank," is just the latest in that trend. Of course, it's little surprise that the director behind punchy, stunt-centric movies like "The Fall Guy" or "Atomic Blonde" would opt for a more deliberate approach rather than the simplest one. But how do you take that over-the-top stylistic direction and make it work alongside a much more grounded, emotional, and politically relevant storyline?.

Diungkapkan bahwa fortunately, i had the chance to ask leitch about how he pulled this off in "how to rob a bank" during a recent press junket. As it turns out, balancing two such divergent tones presented its own unique problem that had to be solved creatively. For Leitch, it was a matter of delineating between both aspects of writer Mark Bianculli's script and having form follow function:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "there were two very different visual stories we were telling. Then you had these bombastic episodes of this charismatic content creator. Actually, the challenge opportunity was exciting to bring them together. We were telling the grounded story of these characters and their very relatable plights that are happening, that are a snapshot of our times. And we shot that on 35 millimeter and there was a very traditional visual style we chose intentionally for that. And then the challenge was bringing those two worlds together. ".

In fact, Leitch pinpoints the moment where these worlds finally collide.

Diungkapkan bahwa as much as "how to rob a bank" presents itself as a rollicking, thrill-a-minute roller coaster ride, things take an abrupt turn an hour in. Reilly's FBI Agent John West) track down their identities, and they soon land on opposite sides of an interrogation room. Our gang of bank-robbing Robin Hoods make a key mistake, their dogged pursuers (led by Zoë Kravitz's tech-wiz Reagan and John C. But, as the leader of this pack, Ryan has never found a setback he can't turn into a teachable moment — or, more cynically, a piece of content.

Diungkapkan bahwa that's exactly what happens here, when both halves of the movie come into focus. "I think where we do it really well, and it's my favorite scene in the movie," David Leitch explains to me, "is during the interrogation sequence, where we're blurring the lines between the Wolf's show — basically [explaining] how to survive an interrogation — and the actual footage, being in the real interrogation. " Here, Leitch and his creative team splice together straightforward imagery from the interrogation (which is mostly our defiant characters sitting silently, demanding their lawyer) and imagery where Ryan uses (or imagines?) this as his latest YouTube video: How to Survive an Interrogation.

According to Leitch, this allowed him to play with what we're seeing versus what's really happening:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "even the characters in the movie breaking the fourth wall or texts coming up on the screen when we're in the film, now it's like [the] content creator visual style is changing the way that i'm telling you the narrative aspect of the film. And I'm actually using the narrative aspect of the film to influence the way that I composed the content creator footage. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa despite the complexity in putting this sequence together, all of this is seamlessly cut and presented in a way where it hardly even registers to moviegoers. At the moment, we're too concerned with the fate of Ryan, his lover Emi (Anna Sawai), and the rest of their friends as all their best-laid plans come crashing down. Adding to the tension is the delicate balance of power suddenly shifting away from these honorable thieves trying to make a societal point and towards the man representing all the structural ills they're fighting against: FBI Agent John West.

Diungkapkan bahwa during our conversation, "how to rob a bank" producer and 87north production company founder kelly mccormick chimes in and adds, "that's exactly where the power is shifting and where the worlds are colliding. " Intriguingly, none of this is meant to register to viewers who are (hopefully) absorbed by the storytelling in the moment. So, in a masterful way, [David Leitch is] toying with you there, manipulating you with both ways of storytelling. According to Leitch, this is something that he only conveyed through the subtext and through the visuals in how he and director of photography Jonathan Sela shot the scene:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it's not necessary for the audience to really understand it, but that's the uneasy feeling i'm trying to give, is the power switching. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, we won't give away anything that happens next, but it's safe to say this is the turning point where things kick into another gear. From that point on, the film's stakes are firmly set and nobody feels safe. "How to Rob a Bank" is now playing in theaters.

Diungkapkan bahwa when i was in my late 20s, i lived in the worst building in the best part of soho. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the writer deborah schoeneman introduced me to her best friend from cornell university, who she said would be the perfect roommate. The day she moved in, she gingerly walked up the four flights of stairs carrying a large wrought-iron cage containing a shrieking bird. I figured she wouldn’t be home much while I was, and told her if she had $1,800 a month, she had a deal. Jen Blumin was a Sex and the City character come to life: a tall, gorgeous blonde who managed a high-end event space with a private pool a few blocks away, mostly for corporate sponsors. “Did I not tell you I had a cockatoo?” she asked with such insouciant camp, such mock innocence, that I just had to laugh.

Schoeneman, Grigoriadis, and Blumin in 2010 at Round Hill Resort.

Sebagaimana diketahui, thus began one of my life’s great friendships, proceeding through many more ripostes, a decade of shared living space, and the birth of two kids each. The love of her life and father of her children, the architect James Ramsey, conceived of an idea with Dan Barasch, another Cornell chum, to create a “low line” under the old Delancy Street trolley terminal, and for a while it seemed like that was going to happen. Jen became wildly successful by turning vacant institutional buildings into heart-stopping event spaces, and even landed the contract for New York Fashion Week at the old post office across from Pennsylvania Station. But the relationship fell apart, and then things move very fast in my memory: Jen started to say she disliked New York City and wanted to live full time in the North Fork, a new boyfriend showed up, now she was moving to Puerto Rico for the climate and tax breaks, then she and the boyfriend were buying a private plane to fly direct from Puerto Rico to Islip, NY.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when i heard about this new acquisition by my far-more successful friend, i have to admit i thought it sounded rad. As former Vanity Fair editor Tina Brown wrote on her Substack, everyone wants to be your friend when you have a plane: “The late TV legend Barbara Walters used to lament the necessity to vacation every year with the crass termagant CEO of a bra company just because said termagant happened to own her own plane. Private planes occupy an almost mystical place in our culture. So what if her plane wasn’t the fanciest! It was still glamorous. You’re up in the skies, free of seatmates chomping tuna sandwiches or annoyances like last-minute checked bags. You’re watching the clouds drift by, close enough to touch God. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, for the wealthy, private planes, which have become increasingly popular as a mode of transportation in recent years, aren’t only the ultimate in seclusion, but also the ultimate in spontaneity. You’re in a power position that’s completely the reverse of commercial flights, which reduce you to helpless nose-boned chattel. If you’re paying the bill, most decisions are controlled by you: You decide when you leave, who to invite, what to eat (certainly not pretzels and ginger ale), and whether there’s space for your three bulldogs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but the day after mother’s day in 2017—which jen memorialized by sending a group text to myself and the core girlfriends with a snapshot of her two toddlers on a big rock in puerto rico—jen’s private plane fell out of the sky. She was flying with her children about 15 miles east of Eleuthera, an island in the Bahamas, in the Bermuda Triangle. None of them were found.

Diungkapkan bahwa i think a lot about jen, but rarely more than now, nearly a decade after her death. Adam Robinson, who chartered the Learjet that dove into a Florida road on November 1, leaving hypersurreal audio and video recordings that are now seared into the nation’s collective memory, arrived in New York a little later than Jen. That’s because this month, the same set of New York friends—loosely—are mourning another person who died with his family, including two more children under five years old. I met him in the mid-2000s, but he seemed to be cut from the same cloth as she was: a tall, gregarious Lehman Brothers trader who had inherited a loft on lower Broadway from our mutual friends, the founders of the website College Humor (there was a lot of apartment swapping in lower Manhattan back then).

Sebagaimana diketahui, adam was the definition of a “good guy”: smart, kind, and wry at the right moments. He had the open-hearted self-possession of someone who had traveled widely, but now he was in New York City to start his career, which, like so many of us, involved being hyper-social. He was not a close friend, but I was always happy to see him, and would usually spend 10 minutes at a crowded party chatting before moving on (this means a lot if you, like me, ascribe to the Fitzgeraldian notion that large parties provide intimacy, and prefer not to waste your breath in this rarefied milieu on dolts). A few guys in the crowd were into email marketing, and I heard that Adam had started a business in that industry but didn’t know much about his life after he moved to Austin, nor that he, too, had become quite successful.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s eerie that adam’s private plane was headed to eleuthra, the same area where jen disappeared. They weren’t only trying to make money but to enjoy the money they’d made, and for them, that meant devising a new kind of life. But beyond that coincidence, what I keep returning to is how Jen and Adam’s stage in life had so many similarities: both in their 40s, too early to retire, they had nevertheless entered what you could call the “second phase” of success. That may be okay when you’re traveling in a $75 million G800, or as a guest of Drake in his $185 million plane, or with Kylie Jenner in her $73 million Bombardier, but when you’re on a small plane, it matters. #407. 6 Thriller Miniseries That Are 10/10, No Notes

📅 13 Nov 2026

6 Thriller Miniseries That Are 10/10, No Notes

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/thriller-miniseries-perfect-no-notes/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with its unique ability to let a story unfold over the course of multiple hours while still delivering a succinct resolution that viewers don’t have to wait over the course of multiple seasons to see, the miniseries format has emerged as an outstanding forum for thriller entertainment. Even more impressive is that there has been no shortage of approaches that have worked within the parameters of limited series releases, with everything from action-packed bombast to simmering slow-burn anxiety and even piercing psychological horror having an impact.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these six series stand as true masterpieces of the genre in the format, with everything from murder mystery suspense to puncturing historical tension. Some of these series are universally heralded as being defining masterpieces of limited series drama and television entertainment at large, while others are criminally underrated gems that have never found the recognition and respect they so thoroughly deserve. All of them are faultless forays into small-screen thrills that all lovers of the genre must seek out if they haven’t seen them already.

Berdasarkan laporan, a bold recreation of david cronenberg’s 1988 movie of the same name, dead ringers is a visceral descent into psychologically twisting dread that grounds its heart-stopping suspense in its arresting visuals and rachel weisz’s captivating dual performance. She stars as Beverly and Elliot Mantle, twin sisters who share everything from their career path to lovers, drugs, and a frightful determination to bring their aspirations to life. As they perform ethically questionable procedures on infertile women in preparation for them opening their own independent birthing center, a rift begins to form between the two sisters when Beverly enters into a serious relationship with one of her clients, the famous actress Genevieve Cotard (Britne Oldford).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the amazon prime series is certainly not for the faint of heart, and there have been viewers who voiced their displeasure with its graphic body horror, intentionally unlikable characters, and its abundant, vulgar profanity. However, if audiences can overcome the shocking content and grasp that it is intended to run as a thematically piercing and unrelenting exploration of co-dependency, identity, women’s healthcare, and the power amoral ambition can have when backed by immense wealth, Dead Ringers becomes an intriguing, albeit cold-hearted, viewing experience. Furthermore, it is one of the most fiendishly unsettling miniseries television has seen in many years, making it a must-see gem for genre enthusiasts.

Berdasarkan laporan, a bbc production from the early 2000s that has sadly been completely forgotten over time, state of play is an engrossing mixture of political conspiracy thrills, murder mystery intrigue, and newsroom drama. While investigating the gang-related killing of a teenager, reporter Cal McCaffrey (John Simm) and his colleagues discover a link between the crime and the death of a young political researcher for rising MP, Stephen Collins (David Morrissey). As the newspaper’s investigation pries deeper, they uncover not only the connection of the murders, but a scandalous love affair as well as a conspiracy tying high-ranking British government figures to corruption in the petroleum industry.

Sebagaimana diketahui, written and created by paul abbott and directed by david yates, state of play finds its suspense in its grit and realism. It embeds viewers in the raw, confronting truths of the institutions it explores, from the greed and ambition of political parties to the amoral, story-driven sensationalism of news media. This striking sense of ambiguous righteousness and authentic dread is only heightened by the incredible ensemble cast that includes Bill Nighy, James McAvoy, and Kelly Macdonald, the patient yet propulsive six-hour progression of the story, and the razor-sharp nature of the character dynamics and dialogue.

Sebagaimana diketahui, an excellent blending of mystery, suspense, and sci-fi intrigue, devs is one of the best miniseries of the 2020s so far. Unfortunately, its hostile tone of suspicion and corporate cynicism was a far cry from what audiences were craving at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, and it has since faded from memory. However, the FX/Hulu release is well worth revisiting, with the eight-part miniseries revolving around the mysterious and shocking death of a newly promoted employee, and the endeavor of Lily Chan (Sonoya Mizuno)—the deceased’s colleague and romantic partner—to figure out the truth behind Amaya and its enigmatic CEO, Forest (Nick Offerman).

Diungkapkan bahwa written, directed, and created by alex garland, devs combines its patient and meticulous pacing with an overwhelming sense of thematic gravitas. Lily’s investigation doesn’t just examine the nature of corporate secrecy and professional malpractice; it revels in the depths of such ideas as determinism and free will, theories of multiverses and alternate realities, and the piercing influence of grief and the search for absolution. Complimented by astonishing production design, a uniquely haunting soundscape comprised of expressionistic quantum computer sounds and its eerie score, and the layered complexity of the performances, Devs stands as a sorely overlooked thriller that blends techno-thriller boldness with philosophical depth and mystery suspense to perfection.

Diungkapkan bahwa using the murder mystery format as a platform for piercing character drama and introspective thematic journeys rather than simply as a tightly-paced whodunit thriller, sharp objects stands as one of the more psychologically impressionable miniseries in recent years. Based on Gillian Flynn’s novel, it follows crime reporter Camille Preaker (Amy Adams) as she returns to her hometown of Wind Gap, Missouri, to investigate the murders of two young girls. As she investigates the disturbing case, she must also navigate the re-emerging traumas of her youth, many of which pertain to her strained relationship with her cruel, socialite mother and her shy half-sister.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the underappreciated hbo miniseries benefits greatly from jean-marc vallée’s direction in all eight episodes, with the consistent vision allowing for the story to unfurl with a methodical majesty against a backdrop of small-town malevolence and eerie southern gothic atmosphere. Even as it flicks between Camille’s investigation and her troubled youth, juxtaposing an adult’s jaded world-weariness against young Camille’s (Sophia Lillis) arduous existence under her domineering mother, Sharp Objects maintains a patient though propulsive drive, one defined by a litany of shocking plot twists and outstanding performances from all involved.

Berdasarkan laporan, most miniseries that excel do so by mastering one form of storytelling. It initially runs as a framed innocent man thriller with murder mystery inflections, following Pakistani-American youth Nasir (Riz Ahmed) as he awakens after a night of partying to find his date has been stabbed to death. The Night Of effectively perfects four different subgenres of crime suspense throughout its eight-episode run. As he stands trial and awaits prosecution, the series incorporates courtroom thrills and prison yard tension into the fold, while dogged defense attorney John Stone’s (John Turturro) story mixes investigative lawyer case work with a certain social commentary about wealth and corporate power.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the miniseries as a whole runs as a transfixing crime thriller that asks demanding questions about the integrity and fairness of america’s legal system. This rousing thematic focus is brilliantly supported by exceptional performances and stunning cinematic visuals that exude a sense of simmering, slow-burning intensity. The novelistic ambition of The Night Of as both a character-focused drama and a skewering critique of criminal justice institutions is remarkable, making for a flawless masterpiece of crime thriller television that, even 10 years on from its release, remains an underrated gem from HBO.

Berdasarkan laporan, it may not immediately spring to mind when one thinks of television thrillers—after all, it is defined as being a historical drama—but it is difficult to name a more relentlessly intense and agonizingly suspenseful miniseries than chernobyl. A defining masterpiece of HBO’s production prowess, it explores the aftermath of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant disaster of 1986, covering the horrific experiences of the unsuspecting first responders, the enormity of the operation to contain the radioactive fallout, and the scheming of the Soviet leaders to conceal the true scale of the catastrophe from the world.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the series excels as a commentary on political corruption, an ode to the heroes who sacrificed their lives to restrict the fallout, and an eye-opening cautionary tale of the dangers of nuclear power, but chernobyl is best remembered by many for its ferocious sense of tension. Much of it comes because the audiences know the devastating scope of the reactor meltdown, whereas the characters are examining it as it happens, an approach that makes the inescapable threat of radiation poisoning feel like a damning certainty, a stalking, invisible monster. The ticking clock of objectives that must be completed only heightens this sense of fatalistic dread, especially as the desperate stakes are only interrupted by the folly of bureaucratic process. Great performances and rousing thematic sharpness are the icing on the cake, consolidating Chernobyl as the most gripping and grueling television thriller of all time, miniseries or otherwise.

#408. 37 Years Later, Dolly Parton's Steel Magnolias Line Is Still The Greatest Quote On Grief

📅 13 Nov 2026

37 Years Later, Dolly Parton's Steel Magnolias Line Is Still The Greatest Quote On Grief

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2314007/dolly-parton-steel-magnolias-lin-greatest-quote-grief/

Berdasarkan laporan, "steel magnolias" is one of those movies that always seems to be perpetually playing on television, not unlike the best picture oscar-winning "forrest gump. " Both movies also take place in the South, depicting the trials and tribulations of characters in small towns as they confront the challenges of life, love, and loss.

Diungkapkan bahwa but whereas "forrest gump" follows a single man on his journey across touchstones of the history of the u. S. , "Steel Magnolias" keeps the story isolated to a group of women played by Sally Field, Shirley MacLaine, Daryl Hannah, Olympia Dukakis, Julia Roberts, and the late Dolly Parton. Directed by Herbert Ross and written by Robert Harling, based on his own 1987 stage play of the same name, the film is both tragic and funny as we follow the ups, downs, and in-betweens of these charming and occasionally sassy ladies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, critics were mixed on the movie, with hal hinson of the washington post writing that the film "runs on gags, pitched to the cheapest seats, and maudlin emotion, pitched to the cheapest sentiments. " Meanwhile, Roger Ebert praised the movie, writing, "'Steel Magnolias' is essentially a series of comic one-liners leading up to a teary tragedy, but let it be said that the one-liners are mostly funny and the tragedy deserves most, but not all, of the tears. The script [. ] is on a degenerated line from Tennessee Williams by way of Hallmark cards. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the laughter and the tears are exactly why we're talking about "steel magnolias" now, as it's full of delightful quips and barbs alongside sentiments that might feel like greeting card schmaltz but still pack charm and an emotional punch. That's especially the case when it comes to one of Parton's memorable lines as Truvy Jones, the owner of a home-salon where the Southern women frequently congregate.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the driving forces of "steel magnolias" is julia roberts as shelby eatenton-latcherie, a role for which she earned an academy award nomination for best supporting actress. Shelby has type 1 diabetes, which turns her hope for having children into a health risk. Sadly, as Shelby pursues her motherly desire, the pregnancy damages her kidneys, and she's forced to go on dialysis. But Shelby's mother, Mary Lynn "M'Lynn" Eatenton (Sally Field) is able to donate a kidney to help save her from further grief.

Sebagaimana diketahui, unfortunately, shelby dies due to an infection caused by the suppressive therapy that keeps her body from rejecting the kidney. Stuck unconscious in a hospital, Shelby's family makes the difficult decision to take her off life support.

Diungkapkan bahwa after the funeral, m'lynn is overwhelmed. In a burst of emotion, she swings dramatically through pain, anger, sadness, and disbelief, but then there's a bit of laughter. M'Lynn expresses that she "just wants to hit somebody" until they feel as bad as she does. That's when M'Lynn's friend Clairee Belcher (Olympia Dukakis) offers up Louisa "Ouiser" Boudreaux (Shirley Maclaine) for M'Lynn to punch, much to Ouiser's disbelief and the shock of the other women. It's a hilarious moment that eases the tension and offers some relief.

In the aftermath, M'Lynn apologizes for her emotional outburst, but Truvy offers consolation by saying:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "laughter through tears is my favorite emotion. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, you can see the hallmark-tinged vibe of a line like that, but being cheesy doesn't make it any less true. You don't have to laugh to keep from crying. In the shadow of tragedy, laughing through tears offers a welcome break from the exhaustion of grief. After the death of a loved one, you may even find yourself making dark jokes to cope with the sadness and anger that you feel, and that's okay. Instead, you can laugh through the tears.

Here are some other memorable quotes from "Steel Magnolias," each with its own charm:.

Diungkapkan bahwa "smile! it increases your face value. " — Truvy Jones.

"Well, you know what they say: if you don't have anything nice to say about anybody, come sit by me!" — Clairee Belcher.

"I'm not crazy, I've just been in a very bad mood 40 years!" — Ouiser Boudreaux.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "honey, time marches on, and eventually, you realize it is marchin' across your face. " — Truvy Jones.

Berdasarkan laporan, "the only thing that separates us from the animals is our ability to accessorize. " — Clairee Belcher.

Berdasarkan laporan, "i would rather have 30 minutes of wonderful than a lifetime of nothing special. " — Shelby Eatenton-Latcherie.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "a dirty mind is a terrible thing to waste. " — Ouiser Boudreaux.

Berdasarkan laporan, "i have a strict policy that nobody cries alone in my presence. " — Truvy Jones.
